title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第四十四 桓彝 Volume 74 Biographies 44: Huan Yi

sentences.zh: 桓彝

translations.literal: Huan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of the genealogical appendix.
translations.idiomatic: Here the text opens the genealogical appendix that follows the chapter heading.

sentences.zh: （子云 云弟豁 豁子石虔 虔子振 虔弟石秀 石民 石生 石綏 石康 豁弟秘 秘弟衝 衝子嗣 嗣子胤 嗣弟謙 謙弟修 徐 甯）〉

translations.literal: (Son: Yun. Yun's younger brother: Huo. Huo's son: Shiqian. Shiqian's son: Zhen. Shiqian's younger brothers: Shi Xiu, Shi Min, Shi Sheng, Shi Sui, and Shi Kang. Huo's younger brother: Mi. Mi's younger brother: Chong. Chong's son: Si. Si's son: Yin. Si's younger brother: Qian. Qian's younger brother: Xiu. Xu. Ning.)〉
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yun; Yun's younger brother was Huo. Huo's son was Shiqian; Shiqian's son was Zhen; Shiqian's brothers included Shi Xiu, Shi Min, Shi Sheng, Shi Sui, and Shi Kang. Huo's younger brother was Mi; Mi's younger brother was Chong. Chong's son was Si; Si's son was Yin; Si's younger brother was Qian; Qian's younger brother was Xiu. The appendix also lists Xu and Ning.

sentences.zh: 桓彝，字茂倫，譙國龍亢人，漢五更榮之九世孫也。

translations.literal: Huan Yi, courtesy name Maolun, was a native of Longkang in the Principality of Qiao and was the ninth-generation descendant of Rong, who had been honored as one of the Han court's Five Elders.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi, whose courtesy name was Maolun, came from Longkang in Qiao commandery. He was the ninth-generation descendant of Rong, who had held the prestigious Five Elders advisory rank under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父顥，官至郎中。

translations.literal: His father Hao rose to the office of Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Hao, reached the rank of langzhong (gentleman of the palace).

sentences.zh: 彝少孤貧，雖簞瓢，處之晏如。

translations.literal: Yi was orphaned young and lived in poverty; though his means were no more than a bamboo basket and gourd ladle, he remained perfectly composed.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned while still young and raised in want, he endured the plainest poverty yet remained unruffled and at ease.

sentences.zh: 性通朗，早獲盛名。

translations.literal: His nature was open and lucid, and he won great fame early.
translations.idiomatic: Open-minded and quick-witted, he earned wide renown while still young.

sentences.zh: 有人倫識鑒，拔才取士，或出於無聞，或得之孩抱，時人方之許、郭。

translations.literal: He possessed judgment of men and could recognize character; in promoting talent he drew men forth whether they were unknown to the world or still in the cradle. People of the time compared him to Xu Shao and Guo Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for reading character and spotting ability, elevating men from obscurity—or discerning merit when they were still children—so contemporaries likened him to Xu Shao and Guo Tai.

sentences.zh: 少與庾亮深交，雅為周顗所重。

translations.literal: In youth he formed a deep friendship with Yu Liang and was greatly respected by Zhou Yi.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was close to Yu Liang and highly regarded by Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 顗嘗歎曰：「茂倫嶔崎曆落，固可笑人也。

translations.literal: Yi once sighed and said, "Maolun is lofty and unconventional—truly a man who invites laughter."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi once remarked with a sigh, "Maolun is strikingly eccentric and altogether remarkable—the sort of man you cannot help but smile at."

sentences.zh: 」起家州主簿。

translations.literal: " He first entered office as clerk of the provincial headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as recording clerk to the provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 赴齊王冏義，拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: He answered the call of righteousness raised by Prince Sima Jiong of Qi and was appointed Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi Sima Jiong raised his loyal army, Huan Yi joined the cause and received appointment as cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 元帝為安東將軍，版行逡遒令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan served as General Who Guards the East, [Huan Yi] received a provisional commission as magistrate of Qunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan-di was General Who Guards the East, Huan Yi was given an interim patent appointment as magistrate of Qunqiu county.

sentences.zh: 尋辟丞相中兵屬，累遷中書郎、尚書吏部郎，名顯朝廷。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as aide to the minister of war on the grand chancellor's staff; he rose in succession to palace attendant of the secretariat and gentleman clerk in the ministry of personnel of the masters of writing, and his reputation shone at court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recruited as an aide in the central army bureau under the grand chancellor, then advanced step by step to palace gentleman of the secretariat and personnel secretary in the ministry of personnel, becoming a conspicuous figure at court.

sentences.zh: 于時王敦擅權，嫌忌士望，彝以疾去職。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Dun wielded unchecked power and envied eminent gentlemen of standing; Yi resigned from office citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun then dominated the government and nursed suspicions toward respected scholar-officials, so Huan Yi stepped down on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 嘗過輿縣，縣宰徐甯字安期，通朗博涉，彝遇之，欣然停留累日，結交而別。

translations.literal: Once, passing through Yu County, he met its magistrate Xu Ning, courtesy name Anqi—an open, learned man—and gladly lingered several days, befriended him, and then went on his way.
translations.idiomatic: On a journey through Yu county he encountered Magistrate Xu Ning (courtesy Anqi), whose breadth of learning matched his generous temper; Huan Yi happily stayed on for days, struck up a friendship, and only then departed.

sentences.zh: 先是，庾亮每屬彝覓一佳吏部，及至都，謂亮曰：「為卿得一吏部矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Liang had repeatedly asked Yi to find an outstanding candidate for the ministry of personnel; when Yi reached the capital he told Liang, "I have obtained a personnel secretary for you."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang had long pressed Huan Yi to locate a truly fine officer for the ministry of personnel; upon arriving in the capital, Huan Yi announced, "I have found your man for the ministry."

sentences.zh: 」亮問所在，彝曰：「人所應有而不必有，人所應無而不必無。

translations.literal: " Liang asked where the man was. Yi replied, "What people expect to possess they may lack; what they expect to lack they may yet possess."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang asked who it was, Huan Yi answered obliquely: "Men assume certain qualities ought always to be present, yet they need not be; they assume others ought never to appear, yet they may."

sentences.zh: 徐寧真海岱清士。

translations.literal: Xu Ning is truly a pure gentleman from the lands between Mount Tai and the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning is the very model of an upright scholar from the Hai-Dai region.

sentences.zh: 」因為敘之，即遷吏部郎，竟曆顯職。

translations.literal: " Yi therefore explained his merits, whereupon [Xu Ning] was promoted to gentleman of the ministry of personnel and eventually rose through a series of prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Having laid out Xu Ning's qualifications, he secured Xu's promotion to gentleman of the ministry of personnel, after which Xu climbed steadily through high office.

sentences.zh: 明帝將伐王敦，拜彝散騎常侍，引參密謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming planned to campaign against Wang Dun, he appointed Yi Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and drew him into secret counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, preparing to move against Wang Dun, named Huan Yi regular attendant of scattered cavalry and pulled him into confidential planning.

sentences.zh: 及敦平，以功封萬寧縣男。

translations.literal: After Dun was crushed, Yi was enfeoffed as baron of Wanning county on account of his service.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Dun had been defeated, Huan Yi was ennobled as baron of Wanning county for his contributions.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹溫嶠上言：「宣城阻帶山川，頻經變亂，宜得望實居之，竊謂桓彝可充其選。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Danyang Wen Qiao memorialized: "Xuancheng lies ringed by mountains and rivers and has repeatedly known turmoil; it requires someone of proven prestige and substance to govern it—in private judgment I believe Huan Yi can fill that role.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao, governor of Danyang, submitted a memorial arguing that Xuancheng's rugged terrain had made it a repeated cockpit of rebellion and that only a man of real stature could hold it—he nominated Huan Yi for the post.

sentences.zh: 」帝手詔曰：「適得太真表如此。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied in his own hand: "I have just received Taizhen's memorial saying this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with an edict in his own brush: "Wen Qiao—Taizhen—has just sent me just such a recommendation."

sentences.zh: 今大事新定，朝廷須才，不有君子，其能國乎！

translations.literal: The great enterprise has only now been secured; the court hungers for talent—without gentlemen of quality, how could the state endure!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is newly stabilized and the capital urgently needs capable men; without true gentlemen to serve it, how can there be a functioning government?

sentences.zh: 方今外務差輕，欲停此事。

translations.literal: External affairs are somewhat lighter at the moment; I wish to set this appointment aside."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier duties are modest for now, so I prefer to defer acting on this proposal."

sentences.zh: 」彝上疏深自捴挹，內外之任並非所堪，但以墳柏在此郡，欲暫結名義，遂補彝宣城內史。

translations.literal: " Yi submitted a memorial declining at length, saying he was fit for neither inner nor outer responsibilities; only because his family graves lay in that commandery did he wish briefly to accept nominal rank—and so he was appointed interior administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi answered with a memorial of earnest self-effacement, insisting that neither central nor regional office suited him and pleading that he wished only a nominal tie to Xuancheng where his ancestors were buried; the court nonetheless named him interior administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 在郡有惠政，為百姓所懷。

translations.literal: In the commandery his rule was benevolent, and the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: There he governed with kindness and won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之亂也，彝糾合義眾，欲赴朝廷。

translations.literal: During Su Jun's rebellion Yi rallied loyal troops intending to march to the court's relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose in revolt, Huan Yi gathered righteous volunteers and prepared to hurry toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 其長史裨惠以郡兵寡弱，山人易擾，可案甲以須後舉。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Bei Hui argued that the commandery's forces were weak, that hill folk were easily provoked, and that they ought to keep their armor folded and wait for a better moment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Bei Hui warned that the county levy was too slight and the mountain population too volatile, urging them to hold their troops in check until a riper opportunity.

sentences.zh: 彝厲色曰：「夫見無禮於其君者，若鷹鸇之逐鳥雀。

translations.literal: Yi said sternly, "When one sees outrage against one's lord, it is like hawks and ospreys hunting sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi answered sharply, "To witness treason against the sovereign and do nothing is like letting raptors tear at songbirds."

sentences.zh: 今社稷危逼，義無晏安。

translations.literal: Now the altars of state stand in peril; on grounds of duty there is no room for ease."
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's altars are besieged; righteousness leaves no space for complacency."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣將軍硃綽討賊別帥於蕪湖，破之。

translations.literal: " He then dispatched General Zhu Chuo to attack the rebels' detached commander at Wuhu and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Zhu Chuo against an enemy column at Wuhu and broke it.

sentences.zh: 彝尋出石硊。

translations.literal: Yi soon advanced out toward Shigui.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he moved his force toward Shigui.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣將軍司馬流先據慈湖，為賊所破，遂長驅徑進。

translations.literal: It happened that the court had first sent General Sima Liu to hold Cihu; Liu was defeated by the rebels, who then drove forward unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile imperial troops had posted General Sima Liu at Cihu ahead of time; the rebels shattered Liu's line and swept ahead without pause.

sentences.zh: 彝以郡無堅城，遂退據廣德。

translations.literal: Because the commandery lacked a defensible city, Yi withdrew to Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no strong walls in the commandery seat, Huan Yi fell back to Guangde.

sentences.zh: 尋王師敗績，彝聞而慷慨流涕，進屯涇縣。

translations.literal: Soon the imperial armies suffered defeat; when Yi heard the news he wept with bitter resolve and advanced to camp at Jing county.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the royal army had been routed, he shed tears of outrage and pushed forward to encamp at Jing county.

sentences.zh: 時州郡多遣使降峻，裨惠又勸彝偽與通和，以紓交至之禍。

translations.literal: Many provinces and commanderies were sending envoys to surrender to Jun; Bei Hui again urged Yi to feign negotiation in order to escape being crushed between converging enemies.
translations.idiomatic: As prefectures across the region capitulated to Su Jun, Bei Hui once more urged a sham truce to spare them from attack on every side.

sentences.zh: 彝曰：「吾受國厚恩，義在致死，焉能忍垢蒙辱與醜逆通問！

translations.literal: Yi said, "I have received lavish favor from the state; my duty is to die for it—how could I swallow shame and traffic with traitors!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi replied, "The throne has treated me generously; honor demands I die in its service—I will not dirty myself bargaining with rebels."

sentences.zh: 如其不濟，此則命也。

translations.literal: If we do not prevail, that will be Heaven's decree."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, let that be fate."

sentences.zh: 」遣將軍俞縱守蘭石。

translations.literal: " He sent General Yu Zong to hold Lanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned General Yu Zong to defend Lanshi.

sentences.zh: 峻遣將韓晃攻之。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched general Han Huang against him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun sent Han Huang to assault the position.

sentences.zh: 縱將敗，左右勸縱退軍。

translations.literal: As defeat loomed, Yu Zong's attendants urged him to pull back.
translations.idiomatic: With collapse imminent, Yu Zong's officers begged him to retreat.

sentences.zh: 縱曰：「吾受桓侯厚恩，本以死報。

translations.literal: Zong said, "I owe Marquis Huan profound kindness; my purpose has always been to repay him with my life.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zong answered, "Marquis Huan showed me deep generosity; I meant from the first to repay him with my death."

sentences.zh: 吾之不可負桓侯，猶桓侯之不負國也。

translations.literal: That I must not betray Marquis Huan matches Marquis Huan's refusal to betray the state."
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot betray him, it is because he would never betray the realm."

sentences.zh: 」遂力戰而死。

translations.literal: " He fought to the last and died.
translations.idiomatic: He battled until he fell.

sentences.zh: 晃因進軍攻彝。

translations.literal: Huang then pressed forward to attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang then advanced against Huan Yi himself.

sentences.zh: 彝固守經年，勢孤力屈。

translations.literal: Yi held out for a full year; isolated and exhausted, his strength gave way.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi resisted for a year, but numbers dwindled and his resources ran dry.

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「彝若降者，當待以優禮。

translations.literal: The rebels proclaimed, "If Yi surrenders, we will honor him with generous treatment."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels offered favorable terms should he capitulate.

sentences.zh: 」將士多勸彝偽降，更思後舉。

translations.literal: Many of his officers urged him to pretend surrender and seek another chance later.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders repeatedly pressed him to yield under false pretenses and plan a second rising.

sentences.zh: 彝不從，辭氣壯烈，志節不撓。

translations.literal: Yi refused; his words rang fierce and his integrity never bent.
translations.idiomatic: He would not hear of it; his tone stayed fierce and his principles unbroken.

sentences.zh: 城陷，為晃所害，年五十三。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was killed by Huang; he was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were breached and Han Huang slew him; he was fifty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 時賊尚未平，諸子並流迸，宣城人紀世和率義故葬之。

translations.literal: The rebels were still unbeaten; his sons had scattered in flight. Ji Shihe of Xuancheng led loyal companions to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebellion continued, his sons were scattered abroad; Ji Shihe, a native of Xuancheng, gathered sympathetic locals and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 賊平，追贈廷尉，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: After the rebellion was crushed he was posthumously honored as minister of justice with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace returned, the court posthumously named him minister of justice and gave him the epithet Jian ("direct").

sentences.zh: 咸安中，改贈太常。

translations.literal: During the Xian'an era the honor was changed to minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ai's Xian'an reign his posthumous office was raised to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 俞縱亦以死節，追贈興古太守。

translations.literal: Yu Zong likewise died faithful to his duty and was posthumously honored as grand administrator of Xinggu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zong was also rewarded posthumously—as grand administrator of Xinggu—for dying loyally in service.

sentences.zh: 初，彝與郭璞善，嘗令璞筮。

translations.literal: Earlier Yi had been friendly with Guo Pu and once asked him to cast the milfoil.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Huan Yi had been close to the diviner Guo Pu and once requested a yarrow reading.

sentences.zh: 卦成，璞以手壞之。

translations.literal: When the hexagram was complete, Pu rubbed it away with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the stalks formed a pattern, Guo Pu swept them aside with his palm.

sentences.zh: 彝問其故。

translations.literal: Yi asked why.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 曰：「卦與吾同。

translations.literal: [Pu] said, "The hexagram matches my own.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu said, "It mirrors my own fate."

sentences.zh: 丈夫當此非命，如何！

translations.literal: For a man of spirit to meet such an untimely end—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: What can any stalwart do when heaven marks him for violent death!"

sentences.zh: 」竟如其言。

translations.literal: " Events unfolded exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 有五子：溫、雲、豁、秘、沖。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Wen, Yun, Huo, Mi, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wen, Yun, Huo, Mi, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 溫別有傳。

translations.literal: Wen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen receives his own biography elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 雲字雲子。

translations.literal: Yun's courtesy name was Yunzi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yun bore the courtesy name Yunzi.

sentences.zh: 初為驃騎何充參軍、尚書郎，不拜。

translations.literal: At first he served as army aide to Cavalry General He Chong and as gentleman of the masters of writing; he declined to take up the latter post.
translations.idiomatic: He began as military aide to He Chong, general of swift cavalry, and was nominated gentleman clerk of the masters of writing but refused to assume the duty.

sentences.zh: 襲爵萬寧男，歷位建武將軍、義成太守。

translations.literal: He inherited the baronage of Wanning and in succession held the posts of general who establishes might and grand administrator of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the Wanning barony and later served as general who establishes might and governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去職。

translations.literal: On the death of his mother he left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，起為江州刺史，稱疾，廬於墓次。

translations.literal: After the burial he was recalled as inspector of Jiang province; claiming illness, he built a mourning hut beside her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Once the funeral rites ended, the court summoned him as inspector of Jiang province, but he pleaded illness and lived in a hut at the graveside instead.

sentences.zh: 詔書敦逼，固辭不行，服闋，然後蒞職。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts pressed him urgently; he steadfastly declined until mourning ended, whereupon he took office.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts forced the issue, yet he held out until the mourning term closed, only then entering upon his duties.

sentences.zh: 加都督司豫二州軍事、領鎮蠻護軍、西陽太守、假節。

translations.literal: He was additionally placed in command of military affairs in Si and Yu provinces, concurrently as colonel who guards the southern tribes, grand administrator of Xiyang, and credential-bearing commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given joint command of Si and Yu provincial forces, serving concurrently as colonel who guards the Man peoples, governor of Xiyang, and credential-bearing officer.

sentences.zh: 雲招集眾力，志在足兵，多所枉濫，眾皆嗟怨。

translations.literal: Yun impressed manpower widely, intent on swelling his army; there was much injustice and abuse, and the populace groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yun drafted manpower ruthlessly to fill his ranks, committing widespread abuses that drew bitter complaints from the people.

sentences.zh: 時溫執權，有司不敢彈劾。

translations.literal: Because Wen held power at the time, responsible offices dared not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: With his brother Huan Wen controlling the court, no inspectorate dared bring charges.

sentences.zh: 升平四年卒，贈平南將軍，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Shengping and was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the south with the epithet Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Emperor Mu's Shengping era (360) and was canonized as general who pacifies the south with the epithet Zhen ("steadfast").

sentences.zh: 子序嗣，官至宣城內史。

translations.literal: His son Xu succeeded him and rose to interior administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Xu eventually became interior administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 苻堅寇蜀，豁遣江夏相竺瑤距之。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian invaded Shu, Huo sent Zhu Yao, governor of Jiangxia, to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's Former Qin armies thrust into Shu; Huan Huo dispatched Zhu Yao, administrator of Jiangxia, to block them.

sentences.zh: 廣漢太守趙長等戰死，瑤引軍退。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Guanghan Zhao Chang and others died in battle; Yao withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang of Guanghan and others perished on the field, forcing Zhu Yao to pull back.

sentences.zh: 頃之，堅又寇涼州，弟沖遣輔國將軍硃序與豁子江州刺史石秀溯流就路，稟節度。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jian struck Liang province; Huo's younger brother Chong detached General Who Supports the State Zhu Xu and Huo's son Shi Xiu—inspector of Jiang province—to ascend the river on assignment and placed them under his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Jian turned against Liangzhou; Huan Chong—Huo's younger brother—sent Zhu Xu, general who supports the state, and Huo's son Shixiu, inspector of Jiang province, upriver on campaign under Huan Huo's overall command.

sentences.zh: 豁遣督護桓羆與序等遊軍沔漢，為涼州聲援。

translations.literal: Huo sent Supervising Protector Huan Pi with Xu and others to maneuver along the Han basin as a diversion supporting Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo also ordered Supervising Protector Huan Pi to lead Zhu Xu's columns on mobile operations along the Han River approaches, pinning enemy attention away from Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而張天錫陷沒，詔遣中書郎王尋之詣豁，諮謀邊事。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Tianxi fell; an edict sent Palace Gentleman Wang Xunzhi to Huo to confer on frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tianxi's domain collapsed, the throne dispatched palace gentleman Wang Xunzhi to Huan Huo's headquarters for strategic talks.

sentences.zh: 豁表以梁州刺史毛憲祖監沔北軍事，兗州刺史硃序為南中郎將、監沔中軍事，鎮襄陽，以固北鄙。

translations.literal: Huo memorialized that Inspector of Liang Province Mao Xianzu should supervise military affairs north of the Han, that Inspector of Yan Province Zhu Xu should be appointed south general of the household and supervise military affairs along the Han while stationed at Xiangyang, thereby securing the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Mao Xianzu, inspector of Liangzhou, to oversee the defense north of the Han, while Zhu Xu, inspector of Yanzhou, should take title as south general of the household, command the middle Han sector from Xiangyang, and bolt the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 太元初，遷征西大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taiyuan era he was promoted to general who conquers the west with independent headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era (376–396) he was elevated to general who conquers the west with authority to open his own bureau.

sentences.zh: 豁上疏固讓曰：「臣聞三台麗天，辰極以之增耀；

translations.literal: Huo submitted a memorial firmly declining: "Your servant has heard that the Three Platforms adorn the heavens and thereby lend added brilliance to the pole star;
translations.idiomatic: In memorializing his refusal, Huan Huo invoked the classical image that the Three Platforms constellation ornaments the sky and magnifies the brilliance of the pole star.

sentences.zh: 論道作弼，王猷以之時邕。

translations.literal: that ministers who discourse upon the Way serve as assistants so that the king's grand designs may harmonize in their season.
translations.idiomatic: Those who expound the dao serve as the ruler's assistants and bring royal planning into timely harmony.

sentences.zh: 必將仰參神契，對揚成務，弘易簡以翼化，暢玄風于宗極。

translations.literal: They must therefore rise to divine concord, answer the summons of state business, extend simplicity to nurture transformation, and diffuse subtle teaching to the ultimate pivot.
translations.idiomatic: They must align with heaven's subtle accord, answer the call of practical affairs, nurture transformation through ease and simplicity, and extend refined virtue from the supreme pivot.

sentences.zh: 故宜明揚仄陋，登庸賢俊，使版築有沖天之舉，渭濱無垂竿之逸。

translations.literal: Hence one should elevate the obscure from humble lanes and appoint the worthy and keen, so that mortar-layered laborers may achieve deeds vaulting to heaven and no recluse idles forever beside the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the throne should raise men from lowly lanes and promote the worthy, so strivers from the mortarworks may rise to heaven-reaching deeds while no sage idles forever with a rod beside the Wei.

sentences.zh: 用乃功濟蒼生，道光千載。

translations.literal: Only thus does merit succor the living multitude and the Way shine across ages.
translations.idiomatic: Only then does achievement rescue the people and dynastic virtue shine across the ages.

sentences.zh: 是以德非時望，成典所不虛授；

translations.literal: Thus if virtue falls short of contemporary esteem, established precedent does not grant hollow titles;
translations.idiomatic: Rank is therefore never hollowly bestowed when virtue lacks the esteem of the age.

sentences.zh: 功微賞厚，賢達不以擬心。

translations.literal: and if merit is slight yet rewards are heavy, the enlightened do not harbor such intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Nor will the worthy abide lavish rewards for slight merit.

sentences.zh: 臣實凡人，量無遠致，階藉門寵，遂叨非據。

translations.literal: Your servant is but an ordinary man without breadth of vision; relying on family favor I have undeservedly grasped high station.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is an ordinary man without far-reaching capacity who has climbed by family distinction into a post beyond his deserts.

sentences.zh: 進不能闡揚皇風，贊明其政道；

translations.literal: Advancing, I cannot clarify imperial transformation or illuminate the arts of rule;
translations.idiomatic: In high office I could not proclaim the transforming royal influence or clarify methods of governance.

sentences.zh: 退不能宣力所蒞，混一華戎。

translations.literal: retreating, I cannot marshal strength in my jurisdiction or unify Chinese and barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: In the field I cannot wield the forces under my command or unite Chinese and frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 屍素積載，庸績莫紀。

translations.literal: Years I have consumed salary yet accomplished nothing worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: For years I have drawn salary without deed worthy of record.

sentences.zh: 是以敢冒成命，歸陳丹款。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare risk declining the settled appointment and lay bare my heartfelt sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I venture to decline this mandate and reveal the sincerity of my heart.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下回神玄覽，追收謬眷，則具瞻革望，臣知所免。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty turn your luminous gaze, recall your mistaken favor, and thereby shift the expectations of all who watch—then your servant may know deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty reconsider this misplaced favor, withdraw it, change what all beneath heaven expect, and grant your servant relief.

sentences.zh: 」竟不許。

translations.literal: " The court refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: The throne would not accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅陷仇池，豁以新野太守吉挹行魏興太守、督護梁州五郡軍事，戍梁州。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian took Qiuichi, Huo appointed Grand Administrator of Xinye Ji Yi acting grand administrator of Weixing and supervising protector over military affairs in five Liang province commanderies to garrison Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian seized Qiuichi, Huan Huo named Ji Yi, grand administrator of Xinye, acting governor of Weixing and supervising protector over military affairs in five Liangzhou commanderies to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 堅陷涪城，梁州刺史楊亮、益州刺史周仲孫並委戍奔潰。

translations.literal: When Jian took Fucheng, Inspector of Liang Province Yang Liang and Inspector of Yi Province Zhou Zhongsun both abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's next strike at Fucheng broke Yang Liang, inspector of Liangzhou, and Zhou Zhongsun, inspector of Yizhou; both bolted from their defenses.

sentences.zh: 豁以威略不振，所在覆敗，又上疏陳謝，固辭，不拜開府。

translations.literal: Because martial prestige had failed and positions everywhere collapsed, Huo again submitted a memorial confessing fault and firmly declined the independent headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his prestige and strategy had failed and posts everywhere had collapsed, he again memorialized in apology and firmly declined to accept independent headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，本官如故，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as minister of works while retaining his substantive offices, with the posthumous epithet Jing ("respectful").
translations.idiomatic: The court added posthumous minister of works to his titles, left his active commissions unchanged, and gave him the epithet Jing.

sentences.zh: 贈錢五十萬，布五百匹，使者持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred thousand cash coins and five hundred bolts of cloth; an envoy bearing imperial credentials supervised the funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: The state furnished half a million in cash and five hundred bolts of cloth, and an accredited envoy oversaw the burial rites.

sentences.zh: 豁時譽雖不及沖，而甚有器度。

translations.literal: Though Huo's reputation among contemporaries never quite matched Chong's, he possessed remarkable breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo never enjoyed quite the acclaim Huan Chong did, yet he carried himself with true magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 但遇強寇，故功業不建。

translations.literal: Only because he repeatedly faced formidable enemies did his deeds fall short of lasting fame.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful foes blocked him at every turn, so his accomplishments never matched his talents.

sentences.zh: 初，豁聞符堅國中有謠云：「誰謂爾堅石打碎。

translations.literal: Earlier Huan Huo heard that in Fu Jian's realm a rhyme ran: "Who calls you hard as stone? Stone itself could be smashed to bits."
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when word reached Huan Huo of a ditty circulating in Former Qin—mocking Fu Jian's name by threatening to "break stone"—

sentences.zh: 」有子二十人，皆以「石」為名以應之。

translations.literal: " He fathered twenty sons and gave every one a name containing the graph "stone" to fulfill the omen.
translations.idiomatic: he responded by naming twenty sons with "stone" in each name, as if answering prophecy.

sentences.zh: 唯石虔、石秀、石民、石生、石綏、石康知名。

translations.literal: Among them Shiqian, Shi Xiu, Shi Min, Shi Sheng, Shi Sui, and Shi Kang alone rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shiqian, Shi Xiu, Shi Min, Shi Sheng, Shi Sui, and Shi Kang became household names.

sentences.zh: 石虔小字鎮惡。

translations.literal: Shiqian's childhood name was Zhen'e ("subdue evil").
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shiqian was known in boyhood as Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 有才幹，趫捷絕倫。

translations.literal: He was capable and uncannily quick and agile.
translations.idiomatic: He combined administrative talent with physical daring no one could match.

sentences.zh: 從父在荊州，於獵圍中見猛善被數箭而伏，諸督將素知其勇，戲令拔箭。

translations.literal: While following his father in Jing Province he joined a hunt: inside the ring lay a fierce beast pierced by several arrows. The commanders, knowing his courage, jokingly told him to pull the shafts free.
translations.idiomatic: During a hunt in Jingzhou he came upon a wounded beast pinned by arrows; officers who knew his daring teased him into stepping up to draw them out.

sentences.zh: 石虔因急往，拔得一箭，猛獸跳，石虔亦跳，高於獸身，猛獸伏，復拔一箭以歸。

translations.literal: Shiqian rushed forward and extracted one arrow; the beast sprang, and he sprang higher; when it crouched again he seized another shaft and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sprang in, yanked a shaft free, leaped above the lunging animal, then snatched a second arrow while it cowered and walked away unharmed.

sentences.zh: 從溫入關。

translations.literal: He accompanied Huan Wen through the passes into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Huan Wen on the campaign into the Guanzhong heartland.

sentences.zh: 沖為苻健所圍，垂沒，石虔躍馬赴之，拔沖於數萬眾之中而還，莫敢抗者。

translations.literal: Chong was surrounded by Fu Jiàn (Founding Emperor of Former Qin, personal name Jian) and nearly destroyed; Shiqian spurred through the enemy host, pulled Chong out amid tens of thousands, and rode back while none dared bar his path.
translations.idiomatic: When Former Qin's founding sovereign Fu Jiàn had Huan Chong hemmed in and all but lost, Shiqian charged through the packed ranks, snatched his uncle free, and galloped out untouched.

sentences.zh: 三軍歎息，威震敵人。

translations.literal: The whole army gasped in awe; his prestige stunned the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers up and down the line murmured in wonder, and enemy troops trembled at the name.

sentences.zh: 時有患虐疾者，謂曰「桓石虔來」以怖之，病者多愈，其見畏如此。

translations.literal: People suffering intermittent fever were told "Huan Shiqian is coming" to frighten the ailment away—many recovered, so deeply was he feared.
translations.idiomatic: Parents scared malaria-stricken children by invoking Shiqian's name; patients often rallied, such terror did he inspire.

sentences.zh: 初，袁真以壽陽叛，石虔以甯遠將軍、南頓太守帥諸將攻之，克其南城。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zhen rebelled from Shouyang, Shiqian—as general who displays might afar and grand administrator of Nandun—led the assault and seized the city's southern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen's revolt at Shouyang drew Shiqian, commanding distant-display general's rank and Nandun's governorship, who stormed and broke its southern defenses.

sentences.zh: 又擊苻堅將王鑒於石橋，獲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: He next attacked Fu Jian's general Wang Jian at Stone Bridge and captured five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Stone Bridge he smashed Wang Jian's Former Qin column and took five hundred mounts.

sentences.zh: 除竟陵太守，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand administrator of Jingling but resigned to mourn his father.
translations.idiomatic: Named governor of Jingling, he stepped down when his father died.

sentences.zh: 尋而苻堅又寇淮南，詔曰：「石虔文武器幹，禦戎有方。

translations.literal: Soon Fu Jian struck Huainan again; an edict declared: "Shiqian unites civil polish with martial competence and knows how to manage frontier foes.
translations.idiomatic: Another invasion from Fu Jian prompted an imperial rescript praising Shiqian's balanced talents and ordering him back to duty despite mourning:

sentences.zh: 古人絕哭，金革弗避，況在餘哀，豈得辭事！

translations.literal: The ancients cut mourning short rather than shirk shield and spear—how much less may lingering grief excuse refusal of office!"
translations.idiomatic: If ancient worthies could sheath grief when bronze drums called, how dare we linger in sorrow?"

sentences.zh: 可授奮威將軍、南平太守。

translations.literal: Invest him as general who rouses might and grand administrator of Nanping."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him general who rouses might and governor of Nanping."

sentences.zh: 」尋進冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he rose to champion general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to champion general.

sentences.zh: 苻堅荊州刺史梁成、襄陽太守閻震率眾入寇竟陵，石虔與弟石民距之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's inspector of Jing Province Liang Cheng and grand administrator of Xiangyang Yan Zhen marched on Jingling; Shiqian and his brother Shi Min opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng and Yan Zhen, serving Fu Jian's Jingzhou command, drove toward Jingling until Shiqian and Shi Min barred their path.

sentences.zh: 賊阻敖水，屯管城。

translations.literal: The rebels held the Ao River line and encamped at Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy blocked the Ao River and fortified Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 石虔設計夜渡水，既濟，賊始覺，力戰破之，進克管城，擒震，斬首七千級，俘獲萬人，馬數百匹，牛羊千頭，具裝鎧三百領。

translations.literal: Shiqian laid a plan to ford by night; once across they surprised the foe, fought through, stormed Guancheng, captured Yan Zhen, took seven thousand heads, ten thousand prisoners, several hundred horses, a thousand head of cattle and sheep, and three hundred suits of barded armor.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian slipped across under cover of darkness, struck before dawn, shattered their camp, seized Yan Zhen, and piled up thousands of captives, livestock, and armored kits.

sentences.zh: 成以輕騎走保襄陽。

translations.literal: Cheng fled with light horse to shelter in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng bolted with his cavalry toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 石虔復領河東太守，進據樊城，逐堅兗州刺史張崇，納降二千家而還。

translations.literal: Shiqian again held concurrent grand administrator of Hedong, pushed into Fancheng, expelled Fu Jian's inspector of Yan Province Zhang Chong, accepted two thousand surrendering households, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Reinvested with Hedong's seal, he advanced on Fancheng, chased off Zhang Chong, absorbed two thousand surrendered families, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 沖卒，石虔以冠軍將軍監豫州揚州五郡軍事、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Chong died, Shiqian—as champion general—supervised military affairs across five commanderies of Yu and Yang provinces and became inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Chong's death he took champion general's rank, oversaw five Yu-Yang commanderies, and assumed the Yu provincial inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he left office to mourn his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned again when his mother passed.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復本位。

translations.literal: When the mourning term ended he resumed his former posts.
translations.idiomatic: After the three years' vigil he returned to his prior duties.

sentences.zh: 久之，命移鎮馬頭，石虔求停曆陽，許之。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was ordered to shift headquarters to Matou; Shiqian asked to remain at Liyang and received approval.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders moved his garrison to Matou, but he persuaded them to let him stay at Liyang instead.

sentences.zh: 太元十三年卒，追贈右將軍。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth Taiyuan year and was posthumously named general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 388 C.E. and was canonized as general of the right.

sentences.zh: 追論平閻震功，進爵作塘侯。

translations.literal: Later review of his victory over Yan Zhen raised his nobility to marquis of Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: A subsequent citation for the Yan Zhen campaign advanced his fief to marquis of Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 第五子誕嗣。

translations.literal: His fifth son Dan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son, Dan, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 誕長兄洪，襄城太守。

translations.literal: Dan's eldest brother Hong served as grand administrator of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's oldest brother Hong governed Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 洪弟振。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's next brother was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 振字道全。

translations.literal: Zhen's courtesy name was Daoquan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen styled himself Daoquan.

sentences.zh: 少果銳，而無行。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and keen but lacked moral restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhen was decisive and fierce yet morally reckless.

sentences.zh: 玄為荊州，以振為揚武將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan commanded Jing Province he appointed Zhen general who displays martial prowess and grand administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan made him martial-display general and Huainan's governor while controlling Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉江夏相，以凶橫見黜。

translations.literal: Transferred to governor of Jiangxia, he lost office for cruelty and bullying.
translations.idiomatic: His vicious temper cost him the Jiangxia post.

sentences.zh: 及玄之敗也，桓謙匿於沮中，振逃于華容之沮中。

translations.literal: After Xuan's defeat Huan Qian hid in the Ju marshes while Zhen fled to the Ju wetlands of Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan fell, Qian vanished into the Ju backwaters and Zhen slipped into Huarong's marshes.

sentences.zh: 玄先令將軍王稚徽戍巴陵，稚徽遣人報振云：「桓欽已克京邑，馮稚等復平尋陽，劉毅諸軍並敗于中路。

translations.literal: Xuan had posted General Wang Zhihui at Baling; Zhihui's messenger told Zhen: "Huan Qin has seized the capital; Feng Zhi and company retook Xunyang; Liu Yi's armies were crushed along the road."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhihui, holding Baling for Xuan, sent a courier claiming that Huan Qin had seized the capital, Feng Zhi had recovered Xunyang, and Liu Yi's army had been shattered on the march.

sentences.zh: 」振大喜。

translations.literal: " Zhen rejoiced wildly.
translations.idiomatic: The fabrication threw Zhen into transports of joy.

sentences.zh: 時安帝在江陵，振乃聚黨數十人襲江陵。

translations.literal: Emperor An was then at Jiangling; Zhen scraped together dozens of followers and struck the city.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor lodged at Jiangling, Zhen struck with a handful of retainers.

sentences.zh: 比至城，有眾二百。

translations.literal: By arrival his band numbered two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: By the walls he had swelled to two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 謙亦聚眾而出，遂陷江陵，迎帝於行宮。

translations.literal: Qian likewise raised troops, they seized Jiangling, and escorted the sovereign from his traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Qian emerged with reinforcements, the city fell, and they fetched Emperor An from his mobile court.

sentences.zh: 振聞桓升死，大怒，將肆逆於帝，謙苦禁之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Zhen learned Huan Sheng had died he raged and meant to murder the emperor until Qian restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: News of Huan Sheng's death nearly drove Zhen to regicide before Qian wrestled him down.

sentences.zh: 遂命群臣，辭以楚祚不終，百姓之心復歸於晉，更奉進璽綬，以琅邪王領徐州刺史，振為都督八州、鎮西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He summoned ministers, declaring Chu rule finished and hearts turning back to Jin; they re-presented the imperial seals, invested the Prince of Langye with Xu Province, and named Zhen area commander over eight provinces, general who guards the west, and inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled officials, proclaimed the revival of Jin legitimacy, handed seals to the Prince of Langye for Xu Province, and claimed eight-province command as western garrison general and Jing inspector.

sentences.zh: 帝侍御左右，皆振之腹心，既而歎曰：「公昔早不用我，遂致此敗。

translations.literal: The emperor's attendants were Zhen's creatures; Zhen sighed, "My lord never used me in time—hence this ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Every face around the emperor belonged to Zhen's clique; he groaned that Xuan should have trusted him earlier—

sentences.zh: 若使公在，我為前鋒，天下不足定。

translations.literal: Had my lord lived and set me on the vanguard, the realm would have been settled with ease.
translations.idiomatic: with Zhen as spearhead they could have mastered the empire.

sentences.zh: 今獨作此，安歸乎！

translations.literal: Now I act alone—where can I turn!"
translations.idiomatic: Left solitary now, he saw no way forward."

sentences.zh: 」遂肆意酒色，暴虐無道，多所殘害。

translations.literal: " He drowned himself in wine and women, ruled with savage cruelty, and slew without number.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he indulged every vice and butchered at whim.

sentences.zh: 振營於江津。

translations.literal: Zhen camped at the Yangzi ford.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched camp at the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守魯宗之自襄陽破振將溫楷於柞溪，進屯紀南。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Nanyang Lu Zongzhi marched from Xiangyang, routed Zhen's general Wen Kai at Zuoxi, and advanced to Jinan south of old Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi swept down from Xiangyang, broke Wen Kai at Zuoxi, and dug in at Jinan.

sentences.zh: 振聞楷敗，留其將馮該守營，自率眾與宗之大戰。

translations.literal: Hearing of Kai's defeat Zhen left Feng Gai to guard the camp and personally attacked Zongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen detached Feng Gai to hold the lines while he threw his main force at Lu Zongzhi.

sentences.zh: 振勇冠三軍，眾莫能禦，宗之敗績。

translations.literal: Zhen's valor topped the army; none could withstand him, and Zongzhi was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fought like a demon until Zongzhi's line collapsed.

sentences.zh: 振追奔，遇宗之單騎於道，弗之識也，乃問宗之所在。

translations.literal: In pursuit he met Zongzhi riding alone, failed to recognize him, and asked where Zongzhi had gone.
translations.idiomatic: Chasing stragglers, he crossed paths with Zongzhi—unrecognized—and demanded the governor's whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 紿曰：「已前走矣。

translations.literal: Zongzhi lied, "He has already ridden ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi coolly pointed him forward.

sentences.zh: 」宗之於是自後而退。

translations.literal: " Zongzhi then slipped away behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zongzhi escaped toward the rear.

sentences.zh: 尋而劉毅等破馮該，平江陵。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Yi and others shattered Feng Gai and recovered Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi soon crushed Feng Gai and reclaimed Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 振聞該敗，眾潰而走。

translations.literal: When Zhen heard Gai had lost, his force dissolved in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Word of Feng Gai's ruin scattered Zhen's host.

sentences.zh: 後與該子宏出自溳城，復襲江陵。

translations.literal: Later he and Feng Gai's son Hong slipped from Yuncheng to raid Jiangling again.
translations.idiomatic: He resurfaced from Yuncheng with Hong and struck Jiangling once more.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史司馬休之奔襄陽，振自號荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Sima Xiuzhi fled to Xiangyang; Zhen proclaimed himself inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi bolted for Xiangyang while Zhen styled himself Jing inspector.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍劉懷肅率甯遠將軍索邈，與振戰于沙橋。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Liu Huaisu led General Who Displays Might Afar Suo Miao against Zhen at Sha Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaisu and Suo Miao met him at Sha Bridge.

sentences.zh: 振兵雖少，左右皆力戰，每一合，振輒瞋目奮擊，眾莫敢當。

translations.literal: Though outnumbered, Zhen's companions fought to the last; each clash saw him glare and hack until none dared face him.
translations.idiomatic: Even with few men he led furious charges that broke every opponent's nerve.

sentences.zh: 振時醉，且中流矢，廣武將軍唐興臨陣斬之。

translations.literal: Drunk and struck by a stray arrow, he fell to General Who Extends Might Tang Xing on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Intoxicated and winged by a chance shaft, he died under Tang Xing's blade.

sentences.zh: 石秀，幼有令名，風韻秀徹，博涉君書尤善《老》《莊》。

translations.literal: Shi Xiu enjoyed a fine reputation from boyhood; his manner was lucid and refined; he read widely and especially cherished the Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shixiu was celebrated young for grace and intellect, steeped in all the masters yet fondest of Daoist classics.

sentences.zh: 常獨處一室，簡于應接，時人方之庾純。

translations.literal: He habitually kept to one chamber and rarely received guests; contemporaries likened him to Yu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly, seldom entertained, and men compared him to the recluse-official Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 甚為簡文帝所重。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen esteemed him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen singled him out for favor.

sentences.zh: 豁為荊州，請為鷹揚將軍、竟陵太守，非其好也。

translations.literal: When Huo governed Jing Province he named him general who displays the hawk's sweep and grand administrator of Jingling—posts Shi Xiu did not relish.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo pressed on him hawk-display generalcy and Jingling's governorship—roles that ill suited his temperament.

sentences.zh: 尋代叔父沖為甯遠將軍、江州刺史、領鎮蠻護軍、西陽太守，居尋陽。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced uncle Chong as general who displays might afar, inspector of Jiang Province, concurrently colonel who guards the Man, grand administrator of Xiyang, residing at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded Huan Chong as distant-display general, Jiang inspector, Man-colonel, and Xiyang governor based at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 性放曠，常弋釣林澤，不以榮爵嬰心。

translations.literal: His temperament was free and easy; he hunted and fished in wild places without letting rank burden him.
translations.idiomatic: He roamed rivers and forests with bow and line, indifferent to titles.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，發則命中。

translations.literal: Expert at mounted archery, he never missed.
translations.idiomatic: On horseback his arrows always found their mark.

sentences.zh: 嘗從沖獵，登九井山，徒旅甚盛，觀者傾坐，石秀未嘗屬目，止嘯詠而已。

translations.literal: Once, following Chong on a hunt up Mount Jiujing amid pomp and crowds, Shi Xiu never glanced at the spectacle—only whistled and recited verses.
translations.idiomatic: During a grand hunt on Mount Jiujing he ignored the spectacle and merely whistled poetry while others gawked.

sentences.zh: 謝安嘗訪以世務，默然不答，安甚怪之。

translations.literal: Xie An once pressed him on state affairs; he stayed silent, which puzzled An greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An's questions on policy met stony silence—utterly baffling to the premier.

sentences.zh: 他日，安以語其從弟嗣，嗣以問之，石秀曰：「世事此公所諳，吾又何言哉！

translations.literal: Later An mentioned it to cousin Si, who asked Shi Xiu; he replied, "That gentleman knows the age's business—what could I add!"
translations.idiomatic: When Si relayed the puzzle, Shixiu answered that Xie An already grasped worldly affairs and needed no lecture from him.

sentences.zh: 」在州五年，以疾去職。

translations.literal: " After five years in the province he resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Five years into his tenure illness became his excuse to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 年四十三卒於家，朝野悼惜之。

translations.literal: He died at home at forty-three; court and countryside mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Death took him at forty-three to widespread lament.

sentences.zh: 追贈後將軍，後改贈太常。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as general of the rear; later raised to minister of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The court first titled him general of the rear, then upgraded the honor to minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子稚玉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhiyu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 玄之篡也，以石秀一門之令，封稚玉為臨沅王。

translations.literal: During Xuan's usurpation the court enfeoffed Zhiyu as prince of Lin'yuan to honor Shi Xiu's house.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne he made Zhiyu prince of Lin'yuan, citing the family's virtue.

sentences.zh: 初，沖遣竟陵太守趙統伐襄陽。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong had ordered Grand Administrator of Jingling Zhao Tong against Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong had once tasked Zhao Tong of Jingling with striking Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 至是，石民復遣兵助之。

translations.literal: Now Shi Min reinforced that effort with more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min now poured additional forces into the same objective.

sentences.zh: 尋而苻堅敗於淮肥，石民遣南陽太守高茂衙山陵。

translations.literal: After Fu Jian's defeat at the Fei River Shi Min sent Grand Administrator of Nanyang Gao Mao to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Following Feishui, Shi Min detailed Gao Mao to shield the southern tombs.

sentences.zh: 時堅雖破敗，而慕容垂等復盛。

translations.literal: Though Fu Jian was ruined, Murong Chui and allies revived their power.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin collapsed yet Murong Chui's party flourished anew.

sentences.zh: 石民遣將軍晏謙伐弘農，賊東中郎將慕容夔降之。

translations.literal: Shi Min dispatched General Yan Qian against Hongnong; enemy east interior general Murong Kui surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qian's column into Hongnong won the capitulation of Murong Kui.

sentences.zh: 始置湖陝二戍。

translations.literal: He first founded paired garrisons at Hu and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He established frontier posts at Hu and Shan.

sentences.zh: 獲關中擔幢伎，以充太樂。

translations.literal: Captives from Guanzhong who performed banner-pole acrobatics were drafted into the imperial music bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Qin entertainers skilled at pole acts were pressed into the court orchestra.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅子丕僭號于河北，謀襲洛陽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's son Pi declared himself emperor north of the river and plotted against Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi's rogue regime beyond the Yellow River eyed Luoyang next.

sentences.zh: 石民遣將軍馮該討之，臨隈斬丕，及其左僕射王孚、吏部尚書苟操等，傳首京都。

translations.literal: Shi Min sent General Feng Gai; at Linwei he executed Pi together with vice-director Wang Fu, minister of personnel Gou Cao, and others, forwarding their heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai cornered Pi at Linwei, removed Wang Fu, Gou Cao, and the rest, and shipped their heads east.

sentences.zh: 而丁零翟遼復侵逼山陵，石民使河南太守馮遵討之。

translations.literal: The Dingling chief Di Liao again menaced the tombs, so Shi Min had Grand Administrator of Henan Feng Zun strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Liao's Dingling riders threatened the mausolea until Feng Zun attacked them.

sentences.zh: 時乞活黃淮自稱并州刺史，與遼共攻長社，眾數千人。

translations.literal: Qi Huo leader Huang Huai styled himself inspector of Bing Province and with Di Liao assaulted Changshe at the head of several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Refugee commander Huang Huai claimed Bing inspectorate rank and joined Di Liao against Changshe with a few thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 石民復遣南平太守郭銓、松滋太守王遐之擊淮，斬之，遼走河北。

translations.literal: Shi Min again sent Grand Administrators Guo Quan of Nanping and Wang Xiazhi of Songzi; they slew Huang Huai and drove Di Liao back across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan and Wang Xiazhi crushed Huang Huai and chased Di Liao north of the river.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，進左將軍。

translations.literal: For cumulative merit he advanced to general of the left.
translations.idiomatic: Those victories earned him general of the left.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without male heirs.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons when he died.

sentences.zh: 石生，隆安中以司徒左長史遷侍中，曆驃騎、太傅長史。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng, during Long'an, rose from senior clerk of the left under the minister of education to palace attendant, then served as chief clerk to the grand marshal and grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Long'an he climbed from left senior clerk of the minister of works to palace attendant and steward under successive marshals and tutors.

sentences.zh: 會稽世子元顯將伐桓玄，石生馳書報玄，玄甚德之。

translations.literal: When Prince Kuaiji's heir Yuan Xian prepared to attack Huan Xuan, Shi Sheng galloped a warning letter to him; Xuan was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing Yuan Xian's strike on Xuan, Shisheng raced a confidential note westward and earned Xuan's lifelong debt.

sentences.zh: 及玄用事，以為前將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Once Xuan dominated the court he appointed Shi Sheng general of the van and inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan repaid him with front general's rank and the Jiang inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He expired still holding those posts.

sentences.zh: 石綏，元顯時為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Shi Sui served as senior clerk of the left under the minister of education during Yuan Xian's ascendancy.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuan Xian's power Shi Sui occupied the left senior clerkship at the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 玄用事，拜黃門郎、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Xuan held power, Shi Sui was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan, Shi Sui became a palace gate attendant and commander of the left palace guard.

sentences.zh: 玄敗，石綏走江西塗中，聚眾攻曆陽，後為梁州刺史傅歆之所殺。

translations.literal: After Xuans defeat Shi Sui fled west of the Yangzi along the highway, gathered followers to attack Liyang, and was later killed by Inspector of Liang Province Fu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sui bolted west of the river, raised rabble against Liyang, and died when Fu Xin struck him down.

sentences.zh: 石康，偏為玄所親愛，玄為荊州，以為振威將軍。

translations.literal: Shi Kang had been singularly dear to Xuan; when Xuan held Jing Province he appointed him General Who Rouses Might.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan favored Shi Kang and, ruling Jingzhou, named him general whose aura shakes the enemy.

sentences.zh: 累遷荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced step by step to Jingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 討庾仄功，封武陵王，事具玄傳。

translations.literal: For merit in the campaign against Yu Ze he was enfeoffed Prince of Wuling; details appear in Xuans biography.
translations.idiomatic: His share in suppressing Yu Ze brought the princedom of Wuling; the fuller story lives in Huan Xuans chapter.

sentences.zh: 秘字穆子。

translations.literal: Mis courtesy name was Muzi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Mi styled himself Muzi.

sentences.zh: 少有才氣，不倫於俗。

translations.literal: In youth he showed talent and spirit and kept apart from vulgar habits.
translations.idiomatic: Young Mi had flair and refused ordinary conformity.

sentences.zh: 初拜秘書郎，兄溫抑而不用。

translations.literal: At first appointed Clerk of the Palace Library, elder brother Wen vetoed the posting and he did not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen blocked his first nomination as imperial librarian.

sentences.zh: 久之，為輔國將軍、宣城內史。

translations.literal: After a long interval he became General Who Supports the State and Interior Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he governed Xuancheng as supporting-state general.

sentences.zh: 時梁州刺史司馬勳叛入蜀，秘以本官監梁益二州征討軍事、假節。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Liang Province Sima Xun rebelled into Shu, Mi in his substantive office supervised military operations in Liang and Yi provinces with credential authority.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xuns invasion of Shu drew Mi into directing Liang-Yi campaigns under interim credentials.

sentences.zh: 勳平，還郡。

translations.literal: Once Xun was pacified he returned to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel collapsed Mi returned to Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎常侍，徙中領軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and was transferred to commander of the household guards.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to scattered-cavalry attendant, then central guard commander.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初即位，妖賊盧竦入宮，秘與左衛將軍殷康俱入擊之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu first ascended the throne the sorcerer-bandit Lu Song broke into the palace; Mi entered together with General of the Left Guard Yin Kang to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Songs palace break-in sent Mi and Yin Kang charging in with the left guard.

sentences.zh: 溫入朝，竊考竦事，收尚書陸始等，罹罪者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Wen entered the capital he secretly investigated the Song affair, seized Masters-of-Writing Lu Shi and others, and many suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wens inquest into Lu Song ensnared Lu Shi and many others.

sentences.zh: 秘亦免官，居於宛陵，每憤憤有不平之色。

translations.literal: Mi too was stripped of office and lived at Waning, nursing visible resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Mi lost rank too and brooded at Waning.

sentences.zh: 溫疾篤，秘與溫子熙、濟等謀共廢沖。

translations.literal: When Wen lay dying Mi plotted with Wens sons Xi and Ji to depose Chong jointly.
translations.idiomatic: At Huan Wens deathbed Mi allied with Xi and Ji to oust Huan Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖密知之，不敢入。

translations.literal: Chong learned of it secretly and dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Chong heard rumors and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 頃溫氣絕，先遣力士拘錄熙、濟，而後臨喪。

translations.literal: The moment Wen expired Chong first dispatched strongmen to seize Xi and Ji, then went to mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had henchmen arrest Xi and Ji as soon as Huan Wen died, then approached the bier.

sentences.zh: 秘於是廢棄，遂居於墓所，放志田園，好遊山水。

translations.literal: Mi was ruined and dismissed; he lived at the cemetery, gave his heart to fields and gardens, and loved roaming mountains and streams.
translations.idiomatic: Ruined, Mi retired among ancestral tombs, farmed, and wandered peaks and rivers.

sentences.zh: 後起為散騎常侍，凡三表自陳。

translations.literal: Later recalled as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, he submitted three memorials declining.
translations.idiomatic: Recall as scattered-cavalry attendant met three refusal memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「秘受遇先朝。

translations.literal: An edict stated: Mi received favor from the prior reign.
translations.idiomatic: The throne noted Mis honors under the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 是以延之。

translations.literal: Therefore we extend him.
translations.idiomatic: So his tenure was prolonged.

sentences.zh: 而頻有讓表，以棲尚告誠，兼有疾疢，省用增歎。

translations.literal: Yet refusal memorials pile up, proclaiming reclusion and sincerity together with illness—reading them adds sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated sick-bed pleas and vows of reclusion moved the emperor to sigh.

sentences.zh: 可順其所執。

translations.literal: Let him follow what he steadfastly holds.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the retirement he seeks."

sentences.zh: 」秘素輕沖，沖時貴盛，秘恥常侍位卑，故不應朝命，與謝安書及詩十首，辭理可觀，其文多引簡文帝之眄遇。

translations.literal: " Mi had always looked down on Chong; Chong was then exalted and powerful, while Mi was ashamed that regular attendant ranked low—thus he ignored court summons, writing Xie An a letter and ten poems of admirable reasoning that cited Emperor Jianwens former favor.
translations.idiomatic: Despising Chongs ascendancy and scorning the low rank of gentleman attendant, Mi shunned office and wrote Xie An verse invoking Emperor Jianwens patronage.

sentences.zh: 先沖卒。

translations.literal: He died before Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He predeceased Chong.

sentences.zh: 長子蔚，官至散騎常侍、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei reached Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General of Irregular Assault.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Wei rose to scattered-cavalry attendant and irregular-assault general.

sentences.zh: 玄篡，以為醴陵王。

translations.literal: At Xuans usurpation Wei was made Prince of Liling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan crowned Wei prince of Liling.

sentences.zh: 沖字幼子，溫諸弟中最淹識，有武幹，溫甚器之。

translations.literal: Chongs courtesy name was Youzi; among Wens younger brothers he was the most broadly learned and possessed military talent; Wen deeply prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong—Youzi—outclassed his brothers in learning and soldiery and won Huan Wens deepest confidence.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太宰、武陵王晞辟，不就。

translations.literal: At the capping age the Grand Tutor, Prince Sima Xi of Wuling, summoned him; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Wuling recruited him at twenty sui; he declined.

sentences.zh: 除鷹揚將軍、鎮蠻護軍、西陽太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Displays the Hawks Sweep, Colonel Who Guards the Man, and Grand Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took hawk-display rank, Man-colonel, and Xiyang governorship.

sentences.zh: 從溫征伐有功，遷督荊州之南陽襄陽新野義陽順陽雍州之京兆揚州之義成七郡軍事、甯朔將軍、義成新野二郡太守，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Following Wen on campaigns he earned merit and was promoted to supervise military affairs in seven commanderies spanning Jing, Yong, and Yang regions as General Who Pacifies the North, concurrently Grand Administrator of Yicheng and Xinye, stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Field service won him pacify-the-north generalcy over seven border commanderies with twin seats at Yicheng and Xinye from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 又從溫破姚襄。

translations.literal: He again followed Wen in defeating Yao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Wen against Yao Xiang and helped break him.

sentences.zh: 及虜周成，進號征虜將軍，賜爵豐城公。

translations.literal: When captive Zhou Cheng was taken his title advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and he received ducal rank at Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Capturing Zhou Cheng earned conquer-the-barbarians generalcy and the Fengcheng ducal patent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷振威將軍、江州刺史、領鎮蠻護軍、西陽譙二郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he shifted to General Who Rouses Might, Inspector of Jiang Province, concurrently Colonel Who Guards the Man and Grand Administrator of Xiyang and Qiao commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated into rousing-might generalcy and Jiang inspector while holding Man-colonel and dual Xiyang-Qiao seats.

sentences.zh: 溫之破姚襄也，獲襄將張駿、楊凝等，徙于尋陽。

translations.literal: When Wen crushed Yao Xiang he captured Xiangs generals Zhang Jun and Yang Ning and relocated them to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun and Yang Ning, Yao Xiangs officers, were resettled at Xunyang after Wens victory.

sentences.zh: 沖在江陵，未及之職，而駿率其徒五百人殺江州督護趙毗，掠武昌府庫，將妻子北叛。

translations.literal: Chong was at Jiangling and had not yet assumed his Jiang post when Zhang Jun led five hundred followers to kill Jiang Provinces Supervising Protector Zhao Pi, loot Wuchangs treasury, and flee north with wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chong reached Jiangzhou, Zhang Jun slew protector Zhao Pi, emptied Wuchang stores, and fled north with families.

sentences.zh: 沖遣將討獲之，遽還所鎮。

translations.literal: Chong sent generals who captured him and hurried back to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Chongs pursuit forces retook Jun and he returned to post.

sentences.zh: 初，彝亡後，沖兄弟並少，家貧，母患，須羊以解，無由得之，溫乃以沖為質。

translations.literal: After Yi died Chong and his brothers were still young, the household poor, and their mother ill—she needed mutton for medicine yet none could be had, so Wen pledged Chong as collateral.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished orphans, the Huans could not buy healing mutton for their mother until Wen pawned young Chong.

sentences.zh: 羊主甚富，言不欲為質，幸為養買德郎，買德郎，沖小字也。

translations.literal: The sheep-owner was wealthy and said he wanted no pawn—only to raise the boy called Maidelan; Maidelan was Chongs childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: The rich shepherd refused collateral but offered to rear the boy nicknamed Maidelan, buyer of virtue.

sentences.zh: 及沖為江州，出射，羊主于堂邊看，沖識之，謂曰：「我買德也。

translations.literal: When Chong became Jiang inspector he went out hunting; the sheep-owner watched from beside the hall and Chong recognized him, saying, I am Maidelan.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, reviewing archery as Jiang inspector, he spotted the old breeder and called himself Maidelan.

sentences.zh: 」遂厚報之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He settled that ancient debt with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進監江荊豫三州之六郡軍事、南中郎將、假節，州郡如故。

translations.literal: Before long he advanced to supervise military affairs across six commanderies of Jiang, Jing, and Yu provinces as South General of the Household with credentials, retaining prior provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion followed to six-commandery command across Jiang-Jing-Yu as south general-of-the-household with credentials.

sentences.zh: 謝安以時望輔政，為群情所歸，沖懼逼，甯康三年，乃解揚州，自求外出。

translations.literal: Xie An, commanding respect of the age, directed policy and drew everyones allegiance; Chong feared pressure and in the third Ningkang year relinquished Yangzhou, seeking assignment outside.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xie Ans grip on court opinion in 375, Chong surrendered Yangzhou for a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 桓氏党與以為非計，莫不扼腕苦諫，郗超亦深止之。

translations.literal: Huan partisans thought it unwise and wrung their wrists in bitter remonstrance; Xi Chao urgently urged against it.
translations.idiomatic: Clan allies protested frantically; Xi Chao begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 沖皆不納，處之澹然，不以為恨，忠言嘉謀，每盡心力。

translations.literal: Chong rejected every plea, remained unruffled and bore no grudge, yet loyal counsel he weighed with full heart.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed objections aside without bitterness yet still heard honest advice.

sentences.zh: 於是改授都督徐兗豫青揚五州之六郡軍事、車騎將軍、徐州刺史，以北中郎府並中軍，鎮京口，假節。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned to supervise military affairs in six commanderies across Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, and Yang provinces as Chariot-and-Horse General and Inspector of Xu Province, merging North General-of-the-Household headquarters with the central army at Jingkou with credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The court shifted him to Xuzhou chariot general commanding six northern commanderies from Jingkou with merged staffs.

sentences.zh: 又詔沖及謝安並加侍中，以甲杖五十人入殿。

translations.literal: An edict further added Chong and Xie An both as palace attendants, permitting fifty armed guards within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Both Chong and Xie An gained palace-attendant rank and fifty halberdiers in the halls.

sentences.zh: 時丹陽尹王蘊以後父之重昵于安，安意欲出蘊為方伯，乃復解沖徐州，直以車騎將軍都督豫江二州之六郡軍事，自京口遷鎮姑熟。

translations.literal: Then Grand Administrator of Danyang Wang Yun, favored as the empress dowagers father, grew intimate with An; An wished to send Yun out as a regional inspector and therefore stripped Chong of Xu Province, naming him Chariot General supervising six commanderies of Yu and Jiang provinces and transferring his seat from Jingkou to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: To ease Wang Yun outward Xie An peeled Xuzhou from Chong and parked him at Gushu over Yu-Jiang theaters.

sentences.zh: 既而苻堅寇涼州，沖遣宣城內史硃序、豫州刺史桓伊率眾向壽陽，淮南太守劉波泛舟淮泗，乘虛致討，以救涼州，乃表曰：

translations.literal: Fu Jian soon raided Liang Province; Chong dispatched Interior Administrator of Xuancheng Zhu Xu and Inspector of Yu Province Huan Yi toward Shouyang while Grand Administrator of Huainan Liu Bo sailed the Huai and Si to exploit gaps and relieve Liangzhou—he therefore memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Facing Fu Jians Liangzhou thrust, Chong aimed Zhu Xu and Huan Yi at Shouyang while Liu Bo rowed the Huai-Si corridor—his memorial opened with

sentences.zh: 氐賊自並東胡，丑類實繁，而蜀漢寡弱，西涼無備，斯誠暴與疾顛，祇速其亡。

translations.literal: the Di rebels having annexed eastern Hu peoples—their vile throngs swarm—while Shu and Han are weak and Western Liang unprepared; such violence coupled with reckless haste only speeds their ruin.
translations.idiomatic: the point that Former Qin Di hosts had absorbed eastern Hu allies while western sectors stayed weak—such rash violence would only hasten collapse.

sentences.zh: 然而天未剿絕，屢為國患。

translations.literal: Still Heaven has not extinguished them and they repeatedly plague the state.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet destroyed them, so they kept wounding the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞勝於無形，功立事表，伐謀之道，兵之上略。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that victory is won before forms take shape and merit stands manifest—subduing the enemys designs is the supreme martial approach.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the adage that winning unseen—by ruining enemy plans—tops every military doctrine.

sentences.zh: 況此賊陸梁，終必越逸。

translations.literal: Moreover these bandits strut defiantly and will ultimately bolt their borders.
translations.idiomatic: Those raiders strutted and would inevitably spill from their own frontier.

sentences.zh: 北狄陵縱，常在秋冬。

translations.literal: Northern Di raid habitually in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: Steppe armies preferred autumn and winter campaigns.

sentences.zh: 今日月迅邁，高風行起，臣輒較量畿甸，守衛重復，又淮泗通流，長江如海，荊楚偏遠，密邇寇仇，方城、漢水無天險之實，而過備之重勢在西門。

translations.literal: Now months race by and north winds rise; I reckon the capital districts doubly guarded, Huai and Si navigable, the Yangzi wide as a sea—Jingchu lies remote yet hugs our foes; Fangcheng and the Han River lack heavens sheer cliff barrier while the weight of defense piles on the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: Days flew; northern gales rose; the capital redoubled its wards while Huai-Si stayed navigable and the Yangzi spread sea-wide—yet Jingzhou hugged the foe without Fangcheng-Han mountain armor, loading the western gate with burden.

sentences.zh: 臣雖凡庸，識乏武略，然猥荷重任，思在投袂。

translations.literal: Though your servant is mediocre and lacks martial stratagem, having undeservedly borne heavy duty my thought is to flap my sleeves and march.
translations.idiomatic: Though modest in talent he burned to roll up sleeves and strike.

sentences.zh: 請率所統，徑進南郡，與征西將軍臣豁參同謀猷。

translations.literal: I ask to lead my command straight into Nan commandery and join Minister Who Conquers the West, your servant Huo, in joint planning.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to drive into Nanjun beside brother Huos western army.

sentences.zh: 賊若果驅犬羊，送死沔漢，庶仰憑正順，因致人利，一舉乘風，掃清氛穢，不復重勞王師，有事三秦，則先帝盛業永隆於聖世，宣武遺志無恨於在昔。

translations.literal: If the foe drives sheep-and-dog levies to die on the Han approaches, perhaps relying on righteous legitimacy we may exploit their mistakes, ride one favorable gale, sweep away their foul vapors, spare the royal army deeper labor, and should affairs touch Guanzhong then the late emperors grand enterprise flourishes forever while Martial Kings testament rests untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: If Fu Jian hurled conscripts onto the Han corridor, Jin could smash them in one wind-borne stroke, easing court burdens and glorifying Gaozu and Xuans martial legacy in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 如其懾憚皇威，窺窬計屈，則觀兵伺釁，更議進取，振旅旋旆，遲速唯宜。

translations.literal: If instead they cower before imperial majesty and schemes fail, we may display arms and watch for openings, reconsider advance, withdraw banners—timing alone should decide.
translations.idiomatic: If they shrank from striking, Jin could probe, wait, and choose pace freely.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下覽臣所陳，特垂聽許。

translations.literal: Humbly I wish Your Majesty to review my words and grant especial consent.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the throne to approve the plan.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「丑類違天，比年縱肆，梁益不守，河西傾喪。

translations.literal: The edict replied: Vile rebels defy Heaven and these years run riot—Liang and Yi fell and Hexi collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The court answered that Di rebels had torn through Liangzhou and the northwest.

sentences.zh: 每惟宇內未一，憤歎盈懷。

translations.literal: Whenever I reflect that the realm is not yet one, indignation fills my breast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admitted rage at continued division.

sentences.zh: 將軍經略深長，思算重復，忠國之誠，形於義旨。

translations.literal: The generals strategy runs deep; plans layer upon layer; loyalty to the state shines in every phrase.
translations.idiomatic: It praised Chongs layered strategy and fervent loyalty.

sentences.zh: 覽省未周，以感以慨。

translations.literal: Reading before finishing I am moved and stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway through the sovereign was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 寇雖乘間竊利，而以無道臨之，黷武窮凶，虐用其眾，滅亡之期，勢何得久！

translations.literal: Though the bandits seize stray gains they rule without the Way, exhaust armies in cruelty, oppress their masses—their date of extinction cannot linger!
translations.idiomatic: Tactical gains could not save a cruel, exhausted tyranny from swift doom.

sentences.zh: 然備豫不虞，軍之善政。

translations.literal: Yet preparedness against surprise is the armies fine governance.
translations.idiomatic: Guard against surprise remained wise soldiery.

sentences.zh: 輒詢於群後，敬從高算。

translations.literal: I have consulted assembled ministers and respectfully follow your lofty calculus.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers endorsed his calculus.

sentences.zh: 想與征西協參令圖，嘉謀遠猷，動靜以聞。

translations.literal: Coordinate with the minister who conquers the west on the chosen plan; share excellent schemes from afar and report every movement.
translations.idiomatic: He should align with Huo and report each move."

sentences.zh: 」會張天錫陷沒，於是罷兵。

translations.literal: " It happened that Zhang Tianxi fell; arms were therefore stood down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxis collapse shelved the attack.

sentences.zh: 俄而豁卒，遷都督江荊梁益寧交廣七州揚州之義成雍州之京兆司州之河東軍事、領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史、持節，將軍、侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon Huo died; Chong was promoted to supervise military affairs across Jiang, Jing, Liang, Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang seven provinces plus Yicheng in Yangzhou, Jingzhao in Yongzhou, and Hedong in Sizhou, concurrently colonel-director of the southern tribes, Inspector of Jing Province, full credentials, retaining general and attendant titles.
translations.idiomatic: Huo death ballooned Chong into seven-province command with satellite theaters, southern-tribes colonelcy, and full Jingzhou powers.

sentences.zh: 又以其子嗣為江州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Si was named Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Son Si inherited the Jiangzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 沖將之鎮，帝餞於西堂，賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: When Chong went to his post the emperor feasted him in the west hall and granted five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign banqueted him in the west hall and gifted half a million cash.

sentences.zh: 又以酒三百四十石、牛五十頭犒賜文武。

translations.literal: He further awarded three hundred forty shi of wine and fifty oxen to civil and military officers.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred forty shi of wine and fifty oxen fed civil and military aides.

sentences.zh: 謝安送至溧洲。

translations.literal: Xie An escorted him to Lizhou ford.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An accompanied him downriver to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 沖既到江陵，時苻堅強盛，沖欲移阻江南，乃上疏曰：「自中興以來，荊州所鎮，隨宜回轉。

translations.literal: Once Chong reached Jiangling Fu Jian stood terribly strong; Chong wished to shift defenses south of the Yangzi and memorialized: Since the restoration Jingzhou headquarters has rotated as convenience dictated.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangling, facing Fu Jians might, Chong argued for sliding the main defense south of the river: since Eastern Jins revival Jingzhou seats had shifted with circumstance.

sentences.zh: 臣亡兄溫以石季龍死，經略中原，因江陵路便，即而鎮之。

translations.literal: My deceased elder brother Wen, when Shi Jilong died, planned the central plains; because Jiangling offered convenient routes, he thereupon stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hus death Huan Wen aimed at the interior and chose Jiangling for logistics.

sentences.zh: 事與時遷，勢無常定。
