translations.literal: Affairs shift with the times; strategic posture has no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances—not maps—should dictate deployment.

sentences.zh: 且兵者詭道，示之以弱，今宜全重江南，輕戍江北。

translations.literal: Moreover war is the way of deception—show weakness; now we ought to mass strength south of the Yangzi and lightly garrison the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: War rewards deceit; mass south of the Yangzi, screen lightly on the north shore.

sentences.zh: 南平孱陵縣界，地名上明，田土膏良，可以資業軍人。

translations.literal: Within Nanping commandery, county Chanling, the place called Shangming has rich soil able to sustain military settlers.
translations.idiomatic: Shangming district in Chanling offered fertile ground to feed garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 在吳時樂鄉城以上四十餘里，北枕大江，西接三峽。

translations.literal: It lies forty-some li upstream from Lexiang city of Wu times, north bordering the great river, west joining the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: It sat forty li above old Wu Lexiang, backing the great river and opening toward the gorges.

sentences.zh: 若狂狡送死，則舊郢以北堅壁不戰，接會濟江，路不雲遠，乘其疲墮，撲翦為易。

translations.literal: If frenzied knaves rush to their deaths, then north of old Ying we hold walls fast without battle; joining forces to cross the river the route is not far; striking their exhaustion and decay is easy.
translations.idiomatic: If enemy hosts hurled themselves north of Ying, Jin could refuse battle behind walls, cross downstream, and crush them fatigued.

sentences.zh: 臣司存閫外，輒隨宜處分。

translations.literal: Your servant holds responsibility beyond the gate and ventures to dispose as fits.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier commander he claimed discretion to execute the shift.

sentences.zh: 」於是移鎮上明，使冠軍將軍劉波守江陵，諮議參軍楊亮守江夏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he shifted headquarters to Shangming, ordered Champion General Liu Bo to hold Jiangling, and advisory aide Yang Liang to hold Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He moved HQ to Shangming, left Liu Bo at Jiangling, and Yang Liang at Jiangxia."

sentences.zh: 詔以荊州水旱饑荒，又沖新移草創，歲運米三十萬斛以供軍資，須年豐乃止。

translations.literal: An edict noted Jingzhou flood-drought famine and Chongs recent move still founding settlements—annual shipment of three hundred thousand hu of grain for army supplies until harvest years return.
translations.idiomatic: The court shipped three hundred thousand hu yearly until famine eased and Chongs new base stabilized.

sentences.zh: 堅遣其將苻融寇樊、鄧，石越寇魯陽，姚萇寇南鄉，韋鐘寇魏興，所在陷沒。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent Fu Rong against Fan and Deng, Shi Yue against Luyang, Yao Chang against Nanxiang, Wei Zhong against Weixing—each place fell.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian hurled Fu Rong, Shi Yue, Yao Chang, and Wei Zhong along separate axes; towns fell everywhere.

sentences.zh: 沖遣江夏相劉奭、南中郎將硃序擊之，而奭畏懦不進，序又為賊所擒。

translations.literal: Chong sent Governor of Jiangxia Liu Shi and South General of the Household Zhu Xu against them; Shi was cowardly and advanced not; Xu was moreover captured by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Chongs riposte faltered: Liu Shi shrank from combat and Zhu Xu fell captive.

sentences.zh: 沖深自咎責，上疏送章節，請解職，不許。

translations.literal: Chong blamed himself deeply, memorialized returning seal and baton requesting dismissal—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong offered resignations the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 遣左衛將軍張玄之詣沖諮謀軍事。

translations.literal: The court sent General of the Left Guard Zhang Xuanzhi to Chong to consult on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Left guard commander Zhang Xuanzhi joined his council.

sentences.zh: 沖率前將軍劉波及兄子振威將軍石民、冠軍將軍石虔等伐苻堅，拔堅築陽。

translations.literal: Chong led Forward General Liu Bo and nephews General Who Rouses Might Shi Min and Champion General Shi Qian against Fu Jian and took Zhuyang from him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Liu Bo, Shi Min, and Shi Qian retook Zhuyang from Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 攻武當，走堅兗州刺史張崇。

translations.literal: He attacked Wudang and put to flight Fu Jians Inspector of Yan Province Zhang Chong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wudang they routed Zhang Chongs Yanzhou column.

sentences.zh: 堅遣慕容垂、毛當寇鄧城，苻熙、石越寇新野。

translations.literal: Fu Jian sent Murong Chui and Mao Dang against Dengcheng, Fu Xi and Shi Yue against Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian answered with Murong Chui and Mao Dang at Dengcheng and Fu Xi plus Shi Yue at Xinye.

sentences.zh: 沖既憚堅眾，又以疾疫，還鎮上明。

translations.literal: Chong both feared Fu Jians numbers and suffered plague; he returned to headquarters at Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered and plague-struck, Chong pulled back to Shangming.

sentences.zh: 表以「夏口江沔衛要，密邇強寇，兄子石民堪居此任，輒版督荊江十郡軍事、振武將軍、襄城太守。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Xiakou where Jiang meets Han is strategically vital hugging the strong foe—his nephew Shi Min can fill the post—and by patent appointed him to supervise ten Jing-Jiang commanderies as General Who Quells Might and Grand Administrator of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated nephew Shi Min for Xiakou command over ten Jing-Jiang counties as quell-might general and Xiangcheng governor.

sentences.zh: 尋陽北接強蠻，西連荊郢，亦一任之要。

translations.literal: Xunyang borders fierce tribes north and links Jing and Ying west—also a key assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyang likewise anchored barbarian-facing frontier with Jing-Ying ties.

sentences.zh: 今府州既分，請以王薈補江州刺史」詔從之。

translations.literal: Now that headquarters and province split he asked Wang Hui be supplemented as Jiang Inspector—edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting staff from province, he proposed Wang Hui for Jiangzhou and won approval."

sentences.zh: 時薈始遭兄劭喪，將葬，辭不欲出。

translations.literal: Wang Hui had just suffered elder brother Shaos death and was about to bury him—declined wishing not to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui cited mourning and declined the tour.

sentences.zh: 於是衛將軍謝安更以中領軍謝輶代之。

translations.literal: Therefore Guard General Xie An instead substituted Central Army Commander Xie You.
translations.idiomatic: Guard general Xie An swapped in central-guard chief Xie You.

sentences.zh: 沖聞之而怒，上疏以為輶文武無堪，求自領江州，帝許之。

translations.literal: Chong hearing this was angry; memorialized that You lacked civil or martial competence and asked personally to hold Jiang Province—the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chong raged at Xie Yous mediocrity and demanded Jiangzhou himself—the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 沖使石虔伐堅襄陽太守閻震，擒之，及大小帥二十九人，送於京都，詔歸沖府。

translations.literal: Chong ordered Shi Qian against Fu Jians Grand Administrator of Xiangyang Yan Zhen, captured him together with twenty-nine lesser leaders, sent them to the capital; edict returned them to Chongs bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qian bagged Yan Zhen plus twenty-nine chiefs; the capital sent the prisoners back to Chongs staff.

sentences.zh: 以平震功，封次子謙宜陽侯。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Yan Zhen his second son Qian was enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan Zhen campaign earned his second son Qian the Yiyang county marquisate.

sentences.zh: 堅使其將郝貴守襄陽，沖使揚威將軍硃綽討之，遂焚燒沔北田稻，拔六百餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had his general Hao Gui defend Xiangyang; Chong sent General Who Displays Might Zhu Chuo against him; they burned the Han north paddies, uprooted over six hundred households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chong ordered Zhu Chuo to scour the northern Han paddies, torching Former Qin crops around Xiangyang and hauling off six hundred families.

sentences.zh: 又遣上庸太守郭寶伐堅魏興太守褚垣、上庸太守段方，並降之。

translations.literal: He further dispatched Grand Administrator of Shangyong Guo Bao against Fu Jians Grand Administrators Chu Yuan of Weixing and Duan Fang of Shangyong; both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Baos column forced Chu Yuan and Duan Fang to capitulate in Weixing and Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 新城太守麹常遁走，三郡皆平。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Xincheng Qu Chang fled; three commanderies were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Chang abandoned Xincheng, rounding out three recovered prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔賜錢百萬，袍表千端。

translations.literal: An edict granted one million cash and a thousand rolls of robe silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with a million cash and a thousand bolts of tribute silk.

sentences.zh: 初，沖之西鎮，以賊寇方強，故移鎮上明，謂江東力弱，正可保固封疆，自守而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chong moved west to his command, because bandits were still powerful he shifted headquarters to Shangming, judging Jiangdong too weak merely to secure existing borders and defend.
translations.idiomatic: First deploying west he evacuated Jiangling for Shangming, judging the southeast able only to husband its frontiers.

sentences.zh: 又以將相異宜，自以德望不逮謝安，故委之內相，而四方鎮捍，以為己任。

translations.literal: Moreover general and minister suited different roles; since his virtue and prestige fell short of Xie Ans he entrusted inner governance to An while charging himself with guarding the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding central policy to Xie An, he kept frontier defense as his own burden.

sentences.zh: 又與硃序款密。

translations.literal: He also grew intimate with Zhu Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated Zhu Xu as confidant.

sentences.zh: 俄而序沒於賊，沖深用愧惋。

translations.literal: Soon Xu fell captive to rebels; Chong felt deep shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xus capture mortified Chong.

sentences.zh: 既而苻堅盡國內侵，沖深以根本為慮，乃遣精銳三千來赴京都。

translations.literal: Then Fu Jian marched the whole realm inward; Chong feared for the dynastic root and dispatched three thousand crack troops toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: National mobilization by Fu Jian pushed Chong to rush three thousand elites eastward to shore up Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 謝安謂三千人不足以為損益，而欲外示閒暇，聞軍在近，固不聽。

translations.literal: Xie An judged three thousand neither helped nor hurt but wished outwardly to show leisure; hearing troops near he firmly refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An waved off the reinforcement as theatrics and barred their entry.

sentences.zh: 報云：「朝廷處分已定，兵革無闕，西籓宜以為防。

translations.literal: He replied: Court disposition is already fixed; weapons need no supplement—the western screen ought itself to defend.
translations.idiomatic: His brush answered that the capital needed no soldiers—the west must guard itself."

sentences.zh: 」時安已遣兄子玄及桓伊等諸軍，沖謂不足以為廢興，召佐吏，對之歎曰：「謝安乃有廟堂之量，不閑將略。

translations.literal: " At that time An had already dispatched nephew Xuan and Huan Yi with various armies; Chong deemed them insufficient for survival or ruin, summoned aides, and sighed to them: Xie An has council-hall capacity yet knows no generalship.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xie An had sortied Xie Xuan and Huan Yi; Chong told staff An possessed cabinet breadth but no battlefield sense—

sentences.zh: 今大敵垂至，方游談不暇，雖遣諸不經事少年，眾又寡弱，天下事可知，吾其左衽矣！

translations.literal: Now with great foe imminent he idles in lofty talk; though he sends inexperienced youths and troops are few and weak, the realms fate is clear—we shall wear barbarian left lapels!
translations.idiomatic: with Fu Jian closing in and boys holding thin lines, Jin would submit to barbarian dress!"

sentences.zh: 」俄而聞堅破，大勳克舉，又知硃序因以得還，沖本疾病，加以慚恥，發病而卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: " Soon word came Fu Jian was shattered, the grand merit achieved, and Zhu Xu thereby returned; Chong was already ill, mortification piled atop shame, and he sickened and died at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Feishi proved him wrong; shame atop chronic illness killed him at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，本官如故，諡曰宣穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored Grand Commandant with substantive offices unchanged; epithet Xuannu ("proclaimed and grave").
translations.idiomatic: The court canonized him grand commandant with epithet Xuannu.

sentences.zh: 賻錢五十萬，布五百匹。

translations.literal: Funeral subvention of five hundred thousand cash and five hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Half a million cash and five hundred bolts accompanied his bier.

sentences.zh: 沖性儉素，而謙虛愛士。

translations.literal: Chongs nature was frugal and plain; he was modest and cherished gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and humble, he favored talented men.

sentences.zh: 嘗浴後，其妻送以新衣，沖大怒，促令持去。

translations.literal: Once after bathing his wife brought new clothes; Chong raged and ordered them taken away.
translations.idiomatic: After a bath his wife offered fresh silks; he barked them away.

sentences.zh: 其妻復送之，而謂曰：「衣不經新，何緣得故！

translations.literal: His wife brought them again, saying, If cloth never knows newness how can it become old!
translations.idiomatic: She insisted garments must be worn new before they age."

sentences.zh: 」沖笑而服之。

translations.literal: " Chong laughed and put them on.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and donned them.

sentences.zh: 命處士南陽劉鄰之為長史，鄰之不屈，親往迎之，禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: He appointed recluse Liu Linzhi of Nanyang chief clerk; Linzhi refused—Chong went personally to welcome him with thick courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to hermit Liu Linzhi as chief clerk, visiting him in person when refused.

sentences.zh: 又辟處士長沙鄧粲為別駕，備禮盡恭。

translations.literal: He also summoned recluse Deng Can of Changsha as aide-de-camp with full ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha recluse Deng Can became aide on elaborate terms.

sentences.zh: 粲感其好賢，乃起應命。

translations.literal: Can, moved by his love of worthies, thereupon rose to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Touched, Deng Can finally took office.

sentences.zh: 初，郗鑒、庾亮、庾翼臨終皆有表，樹置親戚，唯沖獨與謝安書云：「妙靈、靈寶尚小，亡兄寄託不終，以此為恨！

translations.literal: Earlier Xi Jian, Yu Liang, and Yu Yi each left memorials placing relatives in posts; only Chong wrote Xie An: Miaoling and Lingbao are still young; my late brothers trust was not fulfilled to the end—this is my regret!
translations.idiomatic: Unlike peers who nepotized deathbed memos, Chong wrote Xie An only to lament unfinished duty toward infant nephews Miaoling and Lingbao."

sentences.zh: 」言不及私，論者益嘉之。

translations.literal: " His words touched no private gain—critics praised him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Public-minded grief won wider admiration.

sentences.zh: 及喪下江陵，士女老幼皆臨江瞻送，號哭盡哀。

translations.literal: When his bier reached Jiangling, men and women, old and young, came to the river to gaze and send him off, wailing to fullest grief.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling lined the banks weeping as his catafalque passed.

sentences.zh: 後玄篡位，追贈太傅、宣城王。

translations.literal: Later when Xuan usurped, posthumous honors rose to grand tutor and prince of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan later stacked grand tutor and Xuancheng princedom on his ghost.

sentences.zh: 有七子：嗣、謙、修、崇、弘、羨、怡。

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Si, Qian, Xiu, Chong, Hong, Xian, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Seven sons: Si, Qian, Xiu, Chong, Hong, Xian, Yi.

sentences.zh: 嗣字恭祖。

translations.literal: Sis courtesy name was Gongzu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Si styled himself Gongzu.

sentences.zh: 少有清譽，與豁子石秀並為桓氏子侄之冠。

translations.literal: In youth he enjoyed a clean reputation; together with Huos son Shi Xiu he topped the Huan cousins.
translations.idiomatic: Young Si and Shixiu led the cousin generation in repute.

sentences.zh: 沖既代豁西鎮，詔以嗣督荊州之三郡豫州之四郡軍事、建威將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Once Chong replaced Huo in the western command, an edict named Si to supervise military affairs in three Jing commanderies and four Yu commanderies as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Westward succession won Si three Jing and four Yu commanderies under establish-might rank and Jiang inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 蒞事簡約，修所住齋，應作版簷，嗣命以茅代之，版付船官。

translations.literal: His administration was spare; repairing his quarters required plank eaves—Si ordered straw substituted and sent the planks to the boat office.
translations.idiomatic: Building his yamen he swapped costly planks for thatch and recycled timber to the fleet.

sentences.zh: 轉西陽、襄城二郡太守，鎮夏口。

translations.literal: Transferred concurrent Grand Administrator of Xiyang and Xiangcheng, he garrisoned Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Dual Xiyang-Xiangcheng seats anchored Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 後領江夏相，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he held concurrent governorship of Jiangxia and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died holding Jiangxia administrator rank.

sentences.zh: 追贈南中郎將，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored South General of the Household with epithet Jing ("tranquil").
translations.idiomatic: Canonized south interior general with epithet Jing.

sentences.zh: 子胤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yin inherited.

sentences.zh: 胤字茂遠。

translations.literal: Yins courtesy name was Maoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yin styled Maoyuan.

sentences.zh: 少有清操，雖奕世華貴，甚以恬退見稱。

translations.literal: In youth he showed pure conduct; though generations had been noble and honored he was famed for quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Born to glittering rank he prized modest retirement.

sentences.zh: 初拜秘書丞，累遷中書郎、秘書監。

translations.literal: First appointed assistant director of the palace library, he rose to palace gentleman of the secretariat and director of the library.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed from library aide to secretariat gentleman and curator.

sentences.zh: 玄甚欽愛之，遷中書令。

translations.literal: Xuan esteemed him greatly and promoted him palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan elevated him to chief palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 玄篡位，為吏部尚書，隨玄西奔。

translations.literal: At Xuans usurpation he became minister of personnel and fled west with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation made him personnel minister accompanying Xuan west.

sentences.zh: 玄死，歸降。

translations.literal: When Xuan died he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted after Xuans fall.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫善著則祚遠，勳彰故事殊。

translations.literal: An edict stated: When goodness shines, blessings reach far; when merit stands bright precedents differ.
translations.idiomatic: The throne proclaimed that conspicuous virtue reshapes precedent—

sentences.zh: 以宣孟之忠，蒙後晉國；

translations.literal: By Zhao Shuai of Xuans loyalty Later Jin showed grace;
translations.idiomatic: the loyalty of Zhao Dun won Later Jin state indulgence;

sentences.zh: 子文之德，世嗣獲存。

translations.literal: by Ziwens virtue heirs survived whole generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Wens mercy kept heirs alive across reigns.

sentences.zh: 故太尉沖，昔籓陝西，忠誠王室。

translations.literal: Former Grand Commandant Chong once screened Shaanxi in loyalty to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Chong had guarded Shaanxi faithfully—

sentences.zh: 諸子染凶，自貽罪戮。

translations.literal: His sons touched villainy and brought execution on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: yet sons stained themselves in rebellion and died for it—

sentences.zh: 念沖遺勤，用忄妻于懷。

translations.literal: remembering Chongs leftover toil, sorrow lodges in Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: remembering his service still wrings Our heart."

sentences.zh: 其孫胤宜見矜宥，以獎為善。

translations.literal: His grandson Yin ought be pitied and pardoned to reward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Yin deserves mercy to encourage good conduct."

sentences.zh: 可特全生命，徙於新安。

translations.literal: Let his life be spared entire and remove him to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Spare Yin entirely and exile him to Xin'an."

sentences.zh: 」及東陽太守殷仲文、永嘉太守駱球等謀反，陰欲立胤為玄嗣，事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: " When Grand Administrator of Dongyang Yin Zhongwen, Grand Administrator of Yongjia Luo Qiu, and others plotted rebellion, secretly intending to enthrone Yin as Xuans heir, the affair was exposed and they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yin Zhongwen and Luo Qiu schemed to crown Yin as Xuans successor; discovery meant execution."

sentences.zh: 謙字敬祖，詳正有器望。

translations.literal: Qians courtesy name was Jingzu; he was meticulous, upright, and possessed bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian—courtesy Jingzu—was precise, dignified, and commanding.

sentences.zh: 初以父功封宜陽縣開國侯，累遷輔國將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: At first by fathers merit he was enfeoffed founding marquis of Yiyang county; he rose to general who supports the state and interior administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His fathers honors opened Yiyang county marquisate; he rose to supporting-state general and Wu governor.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之亂，謙出奔無錫。

translations.literal: During Sun Ens rebellion Qian fled to Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En drove him to shelter at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 徵拜尚書，驃騎大將軍元顯引為諮議參軍，轉司馬。

translations.literal: Summoned as masters-of-writing gentleman; Grand Marshal Yuan Xian brought him in as advisory aide, then transferred him marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Recall to the ministry paired him as Yuan Xians strategist and chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 元興初，朝廷將伐玄，以桓氏世在陝西，謙父沖有遺惠于荊楚，懼人情向背，乃用謙為持節、都督荊益甯梁四州諸軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史、假節，以安荊楚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxing the court planned to campaign against Xuan; because the Huans had long held Shaanxi and Qians father Chong had left kind memory in Jingchu, fearing popular sentiment might sway, they appointed Qian credential-bearing area commander over Jing, Yi, Ning, and Liang provinces, west general of the household, inspector of Jing Province with credentials, to pacify Jingchu.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of war with Xuan the court named Qian four-province commander and Jing inspector to soothe old Huans retainers.

sentences.zh: 玄既用事，以謙為尚書左僕射，領吏部，加中軍將軍。

translations.literal: Once Xuan held power he made Qian vice-director of the left of the masters of writing, concurrent personnel ministry, plus general of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan made him left vice-director of personnel with central-army rank.

sentences.zh: 謙兄弟顯列，玄甚倚杖之，而內不能善也。

translations.literal: Qian and brothers stood prominent; Xuan leaned heavily on them yet inwardly could not treat them well.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan relied on the brothers yet nursed mistrust.

sentences.zh: 改封謙為甯都侯，拜尚書令，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to marquis of Ningdu; he was appointed masters-of-writing director with addition of regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Titles shifted to Ningdu marquis, minister of education, scattered-cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、衛將軍、開府、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Promoted palace attendant, guard general, independent headquarters, and recorder of masters-of-writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to palace attendant, guard general, independent bureau, and overseer of executive business.

sentences.zh: 玄篡位，復領揚州刺史，本官如故，封新安王。

translations.literal: At Xuans usurpation he again held concurrent inspector of Yang Province with substantive offices unchanged and was enfeoffed prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation brought Yangzhou inspectorate and Xin'an princedom atop prior posts.

sentences.zh: 及桓振作亂，謙保護乘輿，頗有功焉。

translations.literal: When Huan Zhen raised turmoil Qian protected the imperial carriage and won considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhens revolt saw Qian shielding the emperor with credit.

sentences.zh: 然而暗懦，尤不可以造事。

translations.literal: Yet he was dim and timid—especially unable to engineer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet cowardice left him unfit to lead.

sentences.zh: 初，勸振率軍下戰，己守江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier he had urged Zhen to lead troops downstream while he himself held Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted Zhen to strike downstream while he guarded Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 振既輕謙用事，故不從。

translations.literal: Zhen despised Qians wielding power and therefore did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen scorned his cousin and refused.

sentences.zh: 及振敗，謙奔于姚興。

translations.literal: When Zhen was defeated Qian fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat sent Qian to Later Qins Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 先是，譙縱稱籓于姚興，縱與盧循通使，潛相影響，乃表興請謙共順流東下。

translations.literal: Earlier Qiao Zong had declared vassalage to Yao Xing; Zong exchanged envoys with Lu Xun in secret mutual influence; he memorialized Xing requesting Qian jointly descend the river east.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong colluded with Lu Xun and asked Yao Xing to loan Qian for an eastern strike.

sentences.zh: 興問謙，謙曰：「臣門著恩荊楚，從弟玄末雖篡位，皆是逼迫，人神所明。

translations.literal: Xing asked Qian; Qian replied: My house earned gratitude in Jingchu; though cousin Xuan late usurped, all was coercion—men and spirits know this.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned by Yao Xing, Qian pleaded familys Jingzhou virtue and Xuans forced usurpation.

sentences.zh: 今臣與縱東下，百姓自應駭動。

translations.literal: Now if your servant joins Zong eastward the common people will surely be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Marching with Zong would panic the people."

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「小水不容大舟，若縱才力足以濟事，亦不假君為鱗翼。

translations.literal: Xing said: Small waters cannot float large boats—if Zongs talents suffice for the task he needs no fin and wing from you.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing answered that petty streams cannot bear great hulls—if Zong could succeed alone Qian need not help."

sentences.zh: 宜自求多福。

translations.literal: Seek your own blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Seek fortune on your own."

sentences.zh: 」遂遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He let Qian go.

sentences.zh: 謙至蜀，欲虛懷引士，縱疑之，乃置謙于龍格，使人守之。

translations.literal: When Qian reached Shu he wished with open mind to attract gentlemen; Zong suspected him and confined Qian at Longge with guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu Qian tried recruiting talent; Zong jailed him at Longge.

sentences.zh: 謙向諸弟泣曰：「姚主言神矣！

translations.literal: Qian wept to his brothers saying: Lord Yao spoke like a spirit!
translations.idiomatic: He told brothers Yao Xings prophecy proved uncanny!"

sentences.zh: 」後與縱引譙道福俱下，謙於道占募，百姓感沖遺惠，投者二萬人。

translations.literal: Later with Zong he led Qiao Daofu downstream; Qian recruited along the road—common people moved by Chongs old kindness flocked twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward with Zong and Daofu he drafted soldiers; twenty thousand joined remembering Chong.

sentences.zh: 劉道規破謙，斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Daogui defeated Qian and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daogui crushed and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 修字承祖。

translations.literal: Xius courtesy name was Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu styled Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 尚簡文帝女武昌公主，曆吏部郎，稍遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He married Princess Wuchang, Emperor Jianwens daughter; he served as gentleman of the ministry of personnel and gradually rose to general of the left guard.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Wuchang wed him; he rose through personnel secretary to left guard general.

sentences.zh: 王恭將伐譙王尚之，先遣何澹之、孫無終向句容。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong was about to campaign against Prince Qiao Wang Shangzhi he first dispatched He Danzhi and Sun Wuzhong toward Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongs strike on Shangzhi opened with He Danzhi and Sun Wuzhong toward Jurong.

sentences.zh: 修以左衛領振武將軍，與輔國將軍陶無忌距之。

translations.literal: Xiu as left guard concurrently led General Who Quells Might with General Who Supports the State Tao Wuji opposing them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu led left guard and quell-might rank beside Tao Wuji to block them.

sentences.zh: 修次句容。

translations.literal: Xiu encamped at Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: He dug in at Jurong.

sentences.zh: 俄而恭敗，無終遣書求降。

translations.literal: Soon Gong was defeated; Wuzhong sent letters seeking surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gongs fall brought Sun Wuzhongs surrender letters.

sentences.zh: 修既旋軍，而楊佺期已至石頭，時朝廷無備，內外崩駭。

translations.literal: Xiu had already turned his army back when Yang Quanqi reached Stone City; the court was unprepared and court and capital collapsed in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, Xiu found Yang Quanqi at Stone Castle while Jiankang panicked undefended.

sentences.zh: 修進說曰：「殷、桓之下，專恃王恭，恭既破滅，莫不失色。

translations.literal: Xiu advanced counsel saying: Under Yin and Huan all relied on Wang Gong; Gong now destroyed, every face has lost color.
translations.idiomatic: He argued Yin-Kuan factions banked on Wang Gong—Gongs death left them terrified—

sentences.zh: 今若優詔用玄，玄必內喜，則能制仲堪、佺期，使並順命。

translations.literal: Now if a generous edict employs Xuan, Xuan will inwardly rejoice and can control Zhongkan and Quanqi, making both obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: a gracious summons to Huan Xuan would delight him into restraining Yin Zhongkan and Yang Quanqi."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷納之。

translations.literal: The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 以修為龍驤將軍、荊州刺史、假節，權領左衛文武之鎮。

translations.literal: Xiu was named General Who Prances the Dragon, inspector of Jing Province with credentials, acting commander of left guard civil and military at post.
translations.idiomatic: He took dragon-prancer rank, Jing inspectorate, credentials, and temporary left-guard command marching west.

sentences.zh: 又令劉牢之以千人送之。

translations.literal: Liu Lao was also ordered to escort him with one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lao shepherded him with a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 轉仲堪為廣州。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was transferred to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongkan was rotated to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 修未及發，而玄等盟于尋陽，求誅牢之。

translations.literal: Before Xiu could depart Xuan and allies swore covenant at Xunyang demanding Lao be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before departure Xuan bonded at Xunyang to kill Liu Lao.

sentences.zh: 尚之並訴仲堪無罪，獨被降黜。

translations.literal: Shangzhi jointly pleaded Zhongkan guiltless yet alone suffered demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shangzhi protested Zhongkans innocence amid penalties.

sentences.zh: 於是詔復仲堪荊州。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict restored Zhongkan to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Edict restored Zhongkan to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞江績奏修承受楊佺期之言，交通信命，宣傳不盡，以為身計，疑誤朝算，請收付廷尉。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Jiang Ji memorialized that Xiu had embraced Yang Quanqis words, trafficked in secret orders, spread incomplete propaganda, schemed for himself, misled court calculation—request seizure and delivery to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji impeached Xiu for colluding with Quanqi and twisting policy—

sentences.zh: 特詔免官。

translations.literal: A special edict dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: a special rescript only cashiered him.

sentences.zh: 尋代王凝之為中護軍。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Wang Ningzhi as director of palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Wang Ningzhi as central-guard director.

sentences.zh: 頃之，玄破仲堪、佺期，詔以修為征虜將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Xuan crushed Zhongkan and Quanqi; edict named Xiu general who conquers the barbarians and inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan beat Yin and Yang; Xiu became conquer-barbarians general and Jiang inspector.

sentences.zh: 尋復為中護軍。

translations.literal: Soon he again became director of palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regained central guard.

sentences.zh: 玄執政，以修都督六州、右將軍、徐兗二州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: When Xuan held power Xiu was named area commander over six provinces, general of the right, inspector of Xu and Yan provinces with credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan gave him six-province command, right general, Xu-Yan inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 尋進撫軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon promoted general who nurtures the army with addition of regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to nurture-army general plus scattered-cavalry attendant.

sentences.zh: 玄篡，以為撫軍大將軍，封安成王。

translations.literal: At the usurpation he was named Grand General Who Nurtures the Army and enfeoffed Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan made him grand nurture-army general and prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 劉裕義旗起，斬之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yus righteous banner rose [Xiu] was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yus uprising cost him his head.

sentences.zh: 徐寧者，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Xu Ning was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning came from Tan county in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 少知名，為輿縣令。

translations.literal: In youth he was known; he served as magistrate of Yu county.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned young, he governed Yu county.

sentences.zh: 時廷尉桓彝稱有人倫鑒識，彝嘗去職，至廣陵尋親舊，還遇風，停浦中，累日憂悒，因上岸，見一室宇，有似廨署，訪之，雲是輿縣。

translations.literal: At that time Commandant of Justice Huan Yi was famed for judging men; Yi once left office, went to Guangling seeking kin and old friends, and returning met wind—moored mid-channel several days anxious and gloomy—went ashore and saw buildings resembling a yamen; inquiry revealed it was Yu county.
translations.idiomatic: Justice Huan Yi, stranded by weather near Yu county while visiting Guangling, spotted offices ashore and learned he had reached Xu Nings jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 彝乃造之。

translations.literal: Yi therefore paid him a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi went ashore to call.

sentences.zh: 甯清惠博涉，相遇欣然，因留數夕。

translations.literal: Ning was clear-minded, generous, and broadly learned; meeting delighted them and he lingered several nights.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ning welcomed him with calm breadth and kept him days on end.

sentences.zh: 彝大賞之，結交而別。

translations.literal: Yi greatly admired him, formed friendship, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi left impressed and befriended.

sentences.zh: 至都，謂庾亮曰：「吾為卿得一佳吏部郎。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital he told Yu Liang: I have obtained an excellent gentleman for the personnel ministry for you.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he told Yu Liang, I have found your ideal personnel officer."

sentences.zh: 」語在彝傳。

translations.literal: " The account appears in Yis biography.
translations.idiomatic: The tale is told under Huan Yis life."

sentences.zh: 即遷吏部郎、左將軍、江州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He was then promoted gentleman of the ministry of personnel, general of the left, and inspector of Jiang Province, dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to personnel gentleman, left general, and Jiang inspector, dying in harness.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：醨風潛煽，醇源浸竭，遺道德於情性，顯忠信於名教。

translations.literal: The historian says: The wine-weak wind fanned in secret while the pure spring gradually ran dry; the Way and virtue were cast off in disposition while loyalty and trust were paraded in instruction of names.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist laments a culture where thin custom supplants rich virtue and loyalty becomes mere slogan.

sentences.zh: 首陽高節，求仁而得仁；

translations.literal: The lofty integrity at Mount Shouyang sought benevolence and found it;
translations.idiomatic: Boyi-Shuqi purity sought humanity and won it;

sentences.zh: 泗上微言，朝聞而夕死。

translations.literal: subtle words along the Si—hear the Way at dawn and gladly die at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius teaching by the Si promised joy even if life lasted only from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 原軫免胄，懍然於往策；

translations.literal: Xi Yuan doffed his helmet—such stern awe shines from old annals;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chen bared his head in battle—ancient chronicles still thrill at it;

sentences.zh: 季路絕纓，邈矣於前志。

translations.literal: Zilu tied off torn ribbons—remote indeed from earlier intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zilus mercy over fallen caps recalls ideals now distant.

sentences.zh: 況交霜雪於杪歲，晦風雨於將晨，喈響或以變其音，貞柯罕能全其性。

translations.literal: How much more when frost-snow closes the years twilight and wind-rain darkens the coming dawn—harmonious tones may shift their timbre, and rarely does the chaste bough keep its nature whole.
translations.idiomatic: When winter and storm break even steadfast natures may falter.

sentences.zh: 桓茂倫抱中和之氣，懷不撓之節，邁周庾之清塵，遵許郭之遐軌。

translations.literal: Huan Maolun bore a balanced harmony and nursed an unbending integrity; he trod the clear dust of Zhou and Yu and followed the far tracks of Xu and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi joined Zhou Yi and Yu Liangs clarity and rivaled Xu Shao and Guo Tais judgment.

sentences.zh: 懼臨危於取免，知處死之為易，揚芬千載之上，淪骨九泉之下。

translations.literal: Dreading rescue that flees peril, knowing death is the easy path, he spread fragrance a thousand years above and sank his bones below the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: He chose an honorable death over craven life and still shines from the grave.

sentences.zh: 仁者之勇，不其然乎！

translations.literal: Is this not the courage of the benevolent!
translations.idiomatic: That is the valor of a true humane man!

sentences.zh: 至夫基構迭汙隆，龍蛇俱山澤，沖逡巡於內輔，豁陵厲於上游，虔振北門之威，秀坦西陽之務，外有捍城之用，裏無末大之嫌，求之名臣，抑亦可算。

translations.literal: As for foundations that alternately rise and sully, dragon and serpent together in hill and marsh—Chong hesitated as inner bulwark while Huo struck fierce on the upper river, Shiqian and Zhen awed the north gate, Shi Xiu kept Xiyang open—outwardly they served as shielding walls, inwardly no tail-too-large suspicion: counted among famous ministers they may be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huans—Chong steady at court, Huo dominant upstream, Shiqian and kinsmen guarding frontiers, Shixiu easing Xiyang—served the state without overweening power: they rank as true statesmen.

sentences.zh: 而溫為亢極之資，玄遂履霜之業，是知敬仲之美不息檀台之亂，甯俞之忠無救弈棋之禍。

translations.literal: Yet Wen became the fulcrum of excess and Xuan trod the enterprise of treading frost—thus we know Jing Zhongs excellence could not stop the Sandal-Platform turmoil, and Ning Wus loyalty could not avert the chessboard disaster.
translations.idiomatic: But Huan Wens overreach and Xuans usurpation show even Guan Zhong-class talent cannot stop structural collapse, nor Ning Wus faith avert political checkmate.

sentences.zh: 子文之不血食，悲夫！

translations.literal: That Zi Wens line should lack blood sacrifice—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: To end with no heir to tend Zi Wens altar is tragedy enough.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：矯矯宣城，貞心莫陵。

translations.literal: In praise: Lofty, lofty Lord of Xuancheng—no treachery could topple that faithful heart.
translations.idiomatic: Elegy: proud Xuancheng lord, faith unshaken.

sentences.zh: 身隨露夭，名與雲興。

translations.literal: Body perished with dew yet name rose with the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Dust to dust, yet fame ascends like mist.

sentences.zh: 虔豁重世，沖秀雙美。

translations.literal: Shiqian and Huo spanned generations; Chong and Shixiu paired in grace.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian and Huo held generations; Chong and Shixiu twinned in talent.

sentences.zh: 國賴忠臣，家推才子。

translations.literal: The state relied on such loyal ministers; the house boasted such gifted sons.
translations.idiomatic: The realm leaned on their loyalty; the clan on their genius.

sentences.zh: 振武謙文，尋邑為群。

translations.literal: Zhen, military Qian, and Xudang text—soon Xunyang swarmed with their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, the martial Qian, and scribes of their circle soon filled the Xunyang camp.

sentences.zh: 歸之篡亂，曷足以雲。

translations.literal: As for their return to usurpation and chaos—how can that be called worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Their fall into rebellion hardly merits praise."
